You can add a parent by either [saving an item from the web](https://www.zotero.org/support/adding_items_to_zotero) and dragging the PDF on top of it (if a PDF isn’t attached automatically) or by right-clicking on the PDF, choosing Create Parent Item, and entering an identifier such as a DOI or ISBN. If all else fails, you can click Manual Entry after selecting Create Parent Item and manually enter metadata for the item.

## Stored Files and Linked Files [\#](https://www.zotero.org/support/attaching_files\#stored_files_and_linked_files "Permanent link")

Files can be added to your Zotero library as either stored files or linked files.

### Stored Files [\#](https://www.zotero.org/support/attaching_files\#stored_files "Permanent link")

Stored files, which are the default, are stored within the [Zotero data directory](https://www.zotero.org/support/zotero_data), and Zotero will automatically manage them, including deleting them if you delete the attachment item in Zotero. If you use [file syncing](https://www.zotero.org/support/sync), Zotero will automatically sync stored files between devices and make them available in your online library on zotero.org. If you add a stored file from a file on your computer, the file is copied to the Zotero data directory, so you may wish to delete the original to avoid confusion.

When using Zotero file syncing, you can choose to download stored files only as needed, avoiding the need to download all files to every device. An upcoming version of Zotero will allow you to choose how long to keep synced files on a given computer in order to limit disk space usage, temporarily redownloading files when you need them.

To use stored files outside of Zotero, you can use Zotero’s search and organization abilities to quickly find the relevant items and then either drag the attachments straight from Zotero (e.g., into an email) or right-click and choose Show File to view the files in your file manager. If you prefer to find files without going through Zotero, you can use your operating system’s search features (e.g., Spotlight on macOS) or create a smart folder in your OS to show a list of all PDFs within your Zotero data directory and interact with the files directly. Zotero automatically renames files based on the parent item’s bibliographic data, so you can easily find files by title, author, or year even from outside Zotero.

We strongly recommend using stored files for the most seamless experience.

### Linked Files [\#](https://www.zotero.org/support/attaching_files\#linked_files "Permanent link")

With linked files, Zotero only stores a link to the location of the original file on your computer. Linked files are not synced, nor are they deleted if the attachment item is deleted in Zotero. They also can’t be used within a group library, as there’s no guarantee that other group members would have access to the same file location. Linked files are also not supported in the [Zotero iOS app](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/zotero/id1513554812) or the upcoming [Android app](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.zotero.android).

You can add a linked file by selecting an existing item and choosing “Attach Link to File…” from the Add Attachment menu in the Zotero toolbar or, to use [PDF metadata retrieval](https://www.zotero.org/support/retrieve_pdf_metadata), by selecting “Link to File…” from the New Item menu. You can also use the appropriate OS-specific modifier key for linking files while dragging in a file from the filesystem.

If you sync linked files using an external tool (Google Drive, etc.) for use on multiple computers, it is a good idea to set the [linked attachment base directory](https://www.zotero.org/support/preferences/advanced#linked_attachment_base_directory) so that the files can be found by Zotero on each computer even if the containing folder is at a different location in the filesystem.

Given the advanced nature of linked-file workflows, and the differences on individual systems, we’re not able to help troubleshoot problems with specific setups.

If you wish to convert linked files to stored files in order to allow Zotero to manage them, you can do so from the Tools → Manage Attachments menu.

## Adding Files [\#](https://www.zotero.org/support/attaching_files\#adding_files "Permanent link")

### Adding Files via the Browser [\#](https://www.zotero.org/support/attaching_files\#adding_files_via_the_browser "Permanent link")

Zotero can automatically save associated web page snapshots and PDFs when you use the [Zotero Connector save button in your web browser](https://www.zotero.org/support/adding_items_to_zotero#web_translators) (whether associated snapshots and PDFs are saved can be changed in the Zotero [preferences](https://www.zotero.org/support/preferences)). Such snapshots and PDFs are stored as copies in [Zotero data directory](https://www.zotero.org/support/zotero_data), and appear as child items of the saved item.

### Adding Files via the Zotero window [\#](https://www.zotero.org/support/attaching_files\#adding_files_via_the_zotero_window "Permanent link")

#### Drag and Drop [\#](https://www.zotero.org/support/attaching_files\#drag_and_drop "Permanent link")

Files can be copied into your library by dragging a file from your operating system’s file browser into the Zotero window, and either dropping it onto a collection in the left pane, or onto the center pane. Files dropped onto an existing regular Zotero item in the center pane are added as child items. Files dropped onto a collection, or in an empty space or between items in the center pane, are added as standalone items.

You can also drag and drop an existing standalone file item in Zotero onto a regular Zotero item to create a child item.

##### Adding linked files [\#](https://www.zotero.org/support/attaching_files\#adding_linked_files "Permanent link")

- By default, files dragged into Zotero are added as **copies** of the original files. To instead add **links** to the original files, hold down `Ctrl`+`Shift` (Windows/Linux) or `Cmd`+`Option` (Mac) while dropping. (On macOS, it may be necessary to allow the Zotero window to come to the front before letting go for the modifier key to take effect.)

#### New Item Button [\#](https://www.zotero.org/support/attaching_files\#new_item_button "Permanent link")

File copies and file links can be created by clicking the “New Item” (![](https://www.zotero.org/support/_media/add.png)) button at the top of the center column and selecting “Store Copy of File…” or “Link to File…”, respectively. This creates standalone items.

#### Attachment Menu [\#](https://www.zotero.org/support/attaching_files\#attachment_menu "Permanent link")

![](https://www.zotero.org/support/_media/paperclip_dropdown_menu.png)

When you have selected a single item in the center pane, you can click the “Add Attachment” paperclip button at the top of the center column. Select either “Attached Stored Copy of File…” or “Attach Link to File…” to add files as attachments to the item.

You can also “Attach Link to URI…” to add a link to a web page (`http://` or `https://`) or to another program on your computer (e.g., OneNote `onenote://` or Evernote `evernote://`).

These options are also available when you right-click an item and choose “Add Attachment”.

## Accessing Files [\#](https://www.zotero.org/support/attaching_files\#accessing_files "Permanent link")

Files in your library can be accessed by double-clicking the item in the center pane. Alternatively, you can right-click the item and select “View PDF” or “View File”.

To locate a stored (copied) or linked file, right-click the item in the Zotero pane and select “Show File”. Copied files are stored in the [Zotero data directory](https://www.zotero.org/support/zotero_data), and each file has its own subdirectory, which is named with a random 8-character string.

## Web Snapshots [\#](https://www.zotero.org/support/attaching_files\#web_snapshots "Permanent link")

![](https://www.zotero.org/static/images/support/save_button_webpage.png)

Zotero can archive a webpage by creating a snapshot — an offline file reflecting the state of the page at the time the snapshot was taken. If the Zotero Connector does not recognize data on a page, you can save the page as a Web Page item with an attached snapshot by clicking the Zotero save button in the browser toolbar. You can also take a snapshot of any page by right-clicking (click-and-hold in Safari) on the Zotero save button and choosing “Save to Zotero (Web Page with Snapshot)”.

By default, Zotero will save snapshots when importing items from webpages. You can disable this setting in the [Zotero preferences](https://www.zotero.org/support/preferences/general).

entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_batch_execute
entries.description:
Run multiple commands in ONE call. Every command's output is auto-indexed into the knowledge base; if you also pass `queries`, the matching sections come back in the same round trip so a follow-up search call is not needed.

Concurrency parallelizes the FETCH phase (run-the-commands). The DERIVATION phase — turning raw output into an answer — still belongs in code: add a processing command that consumes the indexed output and prints only the answer, so the raw bytes never enter your conversation (Think-in-Code, same principle as the sandbox tool).

WHEN:
  - You have 3+ related commands you would otherwise run sequentially (multi-issue lookups, git log + git diff + git blame, multi-file reads, multi-region cloud queries)
  - You want to gather AND query in one round trip — pass `queries` so the matching sections come back inline
  - You want to parallelize I/O-bound work — pass `concurrency` 2-8 (network calls, gh CLI, cloud APIs, multi-repo git reads)
  - The combined output is large enough that piping it through ctx_search later would itself be expensive — let auto-index + inline queries do both in one shot

WHEN NOT:
  - Single command with no follow-up query — run it in the sandbox tool directly
  - CPU-bound or stateful commands — keep concurrency at 1 (npm test, build, lint, port-binding servers, lock-file holders, anything that races on the same resource)

RETURNS:
  Auto-indexed section list per command label, plus top matches per query (when `queries` is passed). Raw output is NOT echoed in full — only the matched windows. Concurrency>1 switches each command to its own per-command timeout (no shared budget); concurrency=1 preserves the legacy shared-budget cascading-skip-on-timeout path. Use 4-8 for I/O-bound batches; keep at 1 for CPU work or shared-state commands; lower the value when target hosts enforce per-IP rate limits.

EXAMPLE: ctx_batch_execute(
  commands: [
    {label: "issue 1", command: "gh issue view 1"},
    {label: "issue 2", command: "gh issue view 2"},
    {label: "summarize", command: "echo done"}
  ],
  queries: ["root cause", "proposed fix"],
  concurrency: 2
)

label.description: Section header for this command's output (e.g., 'README', 'Package.json', 'Source Tree')

commands.description: Commands to execute as a batch. Output is labeled with the section header. Default order is sequential; pass concurrency>1 to run in parallel (output stays in input order).

queries.description: Search queries to extract information from indexed output. Use 5-8 comprehensive queries. Each returns top 5 matching sections with full content. This is your ONLY chance — put ALL your questions here. No follow-up calls needed.

timeout.description: Max execution time in ms. When omitted, no server-side timer fires — the MCP host's RPC timeout governs. With concurrency=1, the value (when set) is a shared budget across commands; with concurrency>1, it is applied per-command.

concurrency.description: Max commands to run in parallel (1-8, default: 1). Use 4-8 for I/O-bound batches (network, gh, curl, multi-repo git reads). Keep at 1 for CPU-bound (npm test, build, lint) or stateful commands (ports, locks). >1 switches to per-command timeouts (no shared budget) and individual `(timed out)` blocks instead of cascading skip.

cwd.description: Optional working directory for all shell commands in this batch.

query_scope.description: Scope for `queries` (default: `batch`). `batch` searches ONLY the chunks produced by this batch's commands — useful when you want answers about the just-fetched output. `global` searches the entire persistent index (same scope as ctx_search) — useful when you want the batch commands to enrich context and the queries to also surface related prior knowledge in one round trip.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_fetch_and_index
entries.description:
Fetches URL content, converts HTML to markdown (JSON is chunked by key paths, plain text indexed directly), persists it in a searchable knowledge base, and returns a small preview window per source. The raw page bytes never enter your conversation — they live in storage and you retrieve any section on-demand via ctx_search.

Caching: every fetch is cached on disk and reused for repeat calls within the TTL window. The default TTL is 24 hours; override per-call with the `ttl` parameter (milliseconds, `ttl: 0` bypasses cache like `force: true`). Stored content older than 14 days is cleaned up on startup.

WHEN:
  - You need web content (docs, changelogs, API references, spec pages) and the raw page bytes should NOT enter your conversation
  - Multi-URL research (library evaluation, migration scans, doc comparisons): pass the `requests` array and a `concurrency` value 2-8 for parallel I/O
  - You want repeat lookups against the same URL to be cheap (TTL cache hits return only a hint, no re-fetch)
  - You want a long-lived cache window (override `ttl` upward for stable specs) or a guaranteed-fresh fetch (`ttl: 0` or `force: true`)

WHEN NOT:
  - You already have the content locally — store it via the inline index tool
  - The page is SPA-rendered (JavaScript-required to materialize content) — this is a plain HTTP fetch, no headless browser

RETURNS:
  Per-source preview windows extracted around indexable headings plus indexing metadata (chunk counts, source labels, cache state). Raw content is NOT echoed back — retrieve any section on-demand via ctx_search(source: "<label>"). Concurrency parallelizes the fetch phase up to your chosen value (capped by the host's logical CPU count); the FTS5 write phase always runs serially because SQLite is a single-writer store. Net latency = max(fetch latency across the pool) + sum(per-source index write time). Cache hits skip both phases and return a small freshness hint instead of re-fetching. Use 4-8 for stable I/O-bound batches; lower the value when the target host enforces a per-IP rate limit you cannot raise.

EXAMPLE: ctx_fetch_and_index(
  requests: [{url: "https://react.dev/...", source: "react"}, {url: "https://vuejs.org/...", source: "vue"}],
  concurrency: 5
)

url.description: Single URL to fetch and index (legacy single-shape)

source.description: Label for the indexed content when using single `url` (e.g., 'React useEffect docs', 'Supabase Auth API'). For batch, put source in each requests entry.
Label for this URL's indexed content

requests.description: Batch shape: array of {url, source?} entries. Use with concurrency>1 for parallel fetch. Each request indexed under its own source label. Output preserves input order.

concurrency.description: Max URLs to fetch in parallel (1-8, default: 1). Use 4-8 for I/O-bound multi-URL batches (library docs, changelogs, pricing pages). Capped by os.cpus().length on small machines (response notes when capped). Indexing is always serial regardless — only fetches race.

force.description: Skip cache and re-fetch even if content was recently indexed

ttl.description: Override the cache freshness window for this call, in milliseconds. `ttl: 0` bypasses the cache like `force: true`; omit to use the default 24h TTL.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_search
entries.description:
Search a unified knowledge base with a multi-strategy ranking pipeline. Two parallel matchers run on every query: a Porter-stemming matcher ("caching" finds "cached", "caches", "cach") and a trigram-substring matcher ("useEff" finds "useEffect"). Their ranked lists are merged via Reciprocal Rank Fusion, so a document that ranks well in both surfaces above one that wins only on a single strategy. Multi-term queries get an additional proximity-rerank pass that boosts passages where the query terms appear close together. Typos are corrected via Levenshtein distance and re-searched. Result snippets are window-extracted around the matched terms, not blindly truncated.

The knowledge base is unified: queries reach indexed content you stored (ctx_index, ctx_fetch_and_index, ctx_batch_execute output) AND auto-captured session memory written by hooks (decisions, errors, blockers, plans, user prompts, rejected approaches, tool failures, compaction guides — 26 event categories). File-backed sources carry a content hash and auto-flag staleness when the source file changes.

WHEN:
  - You want to recall something that exists in storage (recently indexed content, prior session events, auto-memory) instead of re-reading raw sources
  - You have multiple related questions about the same body of knowledge — batch every question into one call (the ranking pipeline runs per-query but the round-trip cost is paid once)
  - You want to scope the query to one labelled source (pass `source` — partial match is fine)
  - You want a chronological view across current session + prior sessions + persistent auto-memory (pass `sort: "timeline"` — the default `relevance` mode only ranks within the current session)
  - You want to filter ranked results by content shape (pass `contentType: "code"` to surface implementation snippets or `contentType: "prose"` to surface explanations)

WHEN NOT:
  - The data you want to query has never been stored in the knowledge base AND no session memory has accumulated around it — capture first (run a gather-and-index call), then come back here to query
  - You have one ad-hoc question against data that is not in the knowledge base — answer it inline by running code in the sandbox tool; one round-trip instead of capture-then-query

RETURNS:
  Per-query ranked sections with window-extracted snippets. Use 2-4 specific technical terms per query. Common session-memory source labels: `decision` (user corrections / preferences), `error` and `error-resolution` (past failures + their fixes), `blocker`, `plan`, `user-prompt`, `rejected-approach`, `compaction` (post-compact session guide). See ctx_stats for live category counts. Each response carries a throttle counter (call #N/M in the rolling time window); results taper toward the soft cap and calls block after the hard cap. Tune via CONTEXT_MODE_SEARCH_WINDOW_MS, CONTEXT_MODE_SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS_AFTER, CONTEXT_MODE_SEARCH_BLOCK_AFTER.

EXAMPLE: ctx_search(queries: ["root cause", "proposed fix", "test coverage"], source: "issue-#683")
EXAMPLE: ctx_search(queries: ["what did we decide about caching"], source: "decision", sort: "timeline")
EXAMPLE: ctx_search(queries: ["useEffect cleanup pattern"], source: "react-docs", contentType: "code", limit: 5)
EXAMPLE: ctx_search(queries: ["last user prompt", "active skills", "open blockers"], sort: "timeline")

queries.description: Array of search queries. Batch ALL questions in one call.

source.description: Filter to a specific indexed source (partial match).

contentType.description: Filter results by content type: 'code' or 'prose'.

sort.description: Sort mode. 'relevance' (default): BM25 ranked, current session only. 'timeline': chronological across current session, prior sessions, and auto-memory.

project.description: Project scope. Default (omit): this session's project — auto-resolved from the host adapter. 'global': span every project in the shared store (cross-project recall). <absolute-path>: scope to that specific project directory.

--- [current-session | 2026-10-13 15:12 | zotero-duplicates::https://www.zotero.org/support/duplicate_detection] ---
### Duplicate Detection[#](#duplicate_detection "Permanent link") > Merging Duplicates[#](#merging_duplicates "Permanent link")

## Merging Duplicates[#](#merging_duplicates "Permanent link")

You should always resolve duplicate items by merging them, rather than deleting one of the duplicates. Merges will retain all of the collections and tags of the merged items; deleting one item will lose these data. Merges are also automatically recognized by the [word processor plugins](/support/word_processor_integration) and don’t affect your automatically generated citations and bibliographies.

To merge items in the “Duplicate Items” collection, select an item in the center pane. Zotero will automatically co-select the other items that it thinks are duplicates. Click the “Merge <number> Items” button in the right pane to merge the items. If the item fields don’t match completely, you can select one item to be the “master” from the list at the top of the right pane, then select alternative versions of mismatched fields using the icons to the right of each field.

![](/support/_media/duplicate_detection_select.png)

It may be easier to see which items are selected if you [sort the items by Title](/support/sorting). You can select a single item in the “Duplicate Items” view by holding down Alt/Option while clicking. You can de-select an item from a set of duplicates by holding down Ctrl (Windows/Linux) or Cmd (Mac) while clicking.

You can also select a group of two or more items _of the same item type_ anywhere in your Zotero library, right-click, and select “Merge Items…” from the context menu.

On this page

### Duplicate Detection[#](#duplicate_detection "Permanent link") > Finding Duplicates[#](#finding_duplicates "Permanent link")

## Finding Duplicates[#](#finding_duplicates "Permanent link")

Clicking on the “Duplicate Items” collection in your library or right-clicking the library in the left pane and selecting “Show Duplicates” will show the items Zotero thinks are duplicates in the center pane.

![](/support/_media/duplicate_detection.png)

Zotero currently uses the the title, DOI, and ISBN fields to determine duplicates. If these fields match (or are absent), Zotero also compares the years of publication (if they are within a year of each other) and author/creator lists (if at least one author last name plus first initial matches) to determine duplicates. The algorithm will be improved in the future to incorporate other fields.

At this time, it is not possible to mark false positive matches as non-duplicates. This functionality will be added in the future.

Note that duplicate detection only works _within a library_. Items in different group libraries are [separate items](/support/groups#interact_with_groups_through_the_zotero_client). They won’t show up in the “Duplicate Items” collection of any one of the libraries.

### Retrieve PDF Metadata[#](#retrieve_pdf_metadata "Permanent link")

# Retrieve PDF Metadata[#](#retrieve_pdf_metadata "Permanent link")

Users new to Zotero may find the prospect of importing all their data somewhat daunting. Many researchers already have a large collection of PDFs that they’ve previously organized manually. Zotero makes it easy to import these PDFs and retrieve full bibliographic metadata (for searching, citing, indexing, and organizing), taking much of the pain out of switching.

To use this feature, simply drag your existing PDFs into your Zotero library or use the “Store Copy of File” or “Link to File” options from the add new item menu (green plus sign). By default, Zotero will automatically retrieve metadata for each PDF, create an appropriate parent item, and rename the associated file based on the metadata. (You can disable these automatic functions in the [General pane](/support/preferences/general) of Zotero preferences.)

![](https://www.zotero.org/static/images/blog/5.0.36/auto-recognize@2x.gif)

If Zotero can find a match for the PDF, it will create a full Zotero item with the available data and attach the PDF. If it can’t, it will leave the PDF as a standalone attachment, allowing you to add a parent item another way — either by [saving an item from the web](/support/adding_items_to_zotero) and dragging the PDF on top of it or by right-clicking on the PDF, choosing Create Parent Item, and entering an identifier such as a DOI or ISBN. If all else fails, you can click Manual Entry after selecting Create Parent Ite

--- [current-session | 2026-10-13 15:12 | zotero-pdf-metadata::https://www.zotero.org/support/retrieve_pdf_metadata] ---
### Retrieve PDF Metadata[#](#retrieve_pdf_metadata "Permanent link") > How It Works[#](#how_it_works "Permanent link")

### How It Works[#](#how_it_works "Permanent link")

The Retrieve Metadata feature uses a Zotero web service to find item metadata. The Zotero client sends the first few pages of text from the PDF to the web service, which uses a variety of extraction algorithms and known metadata from Crossref, paired with DOI and ISBN lookups, to build a parent item for the PDF. The Zotero lookup service doesn’t require a Zotero account and doesn’t log any data about the content or results of searches.

## Quick Copy[#](#quick_copy "Permanent link")

![quick\_start/rtf-bib\_450x480.png](/support/_media/quick_start/rtf-bib_450x480.png)

If you just want to quickly add references to a paper, email, or blog post, Zotero’s Quick Copy is the easiest way to go. Simply select items in the center column and drag them into any text field. Zotero will automatically create a formatted bibliography for you. To copy citations instead of references, hold down Shift at the start of the drag.

To configure your Quick Copy preferences, open the Zotero [settings](/support/kb/preferences) and select [Export](/support/preferences/export). From this tab you can do the following:

*   Select the export format
*   Set up site-specific export settings
*   Choose whether you want Zotero to include HTML markup when copying

You can also use Edit → Copy Bibliography or press Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-C to copy bibliography entries to your system clipboard and then paste them into documents. To copy citations instead of bibliography entries, use Edit → Copy Citation or Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-A.

In addition to bibliographic output, Quick Copy also supports export formats such as BibTeX and RIS.

## Reporting Style Errors[#](#reporting_style_errors "Permanent link")

If a CSL style doesn’t give the expected output, first make sure that you are running the latest version of Zotero and have the most recent version of the style installed from the [Zotero Style Repository](https://www.zotero.org/styles). Once you have made sure that the style deviates from the style guide, instructions for authors, or published examples, report the error in the [Zotero Forums](/forum). For your post, use the title “Style Error: \[Name of style\]”, and give a link to, or excerpt from, the style guide that shows that the CSL style is wrong. You can also try to [edit the style](/support/dev/citation_styles/style_editing_step-by-step) yourself.

## duplicate items merge fields compare how detection works

--- [current-session | 2026-10-13 15:12 | zotero-duplicates::https://www.zotero.org/support/duplicate_detection] ---
### Duplicate Detection[#](#duplicate_detection "Permanent link") > Merging Duplicates[#](#merging_duplicates "Permanent link")

## Merging Duplicates[#](#merging_duplicates "Permanent link")

You should always resolve duplicate items by merging them, rather than deleting one of the duplicates. Merges will retain all of the collections and tags of the merged items; deleting one item will lose these data. Merges are also automatically recognized by the [word processor plugins](/support/word_processor_integration) and don’t affect your automatically generated citations and bibliographies.

To merge items in the “Duplicate Items” collection, select an item in the center pane. Zotero will automatically co-select the other items that it thinks are duplicates. Click the “Merge <number> Items” button in the right pane to merge the items. If the item fields don’t match completely, you can select one item to be the “master” from the list at the top of the right pane, then select alternative versions of mismatched fields using the icons to the right of each field.

![](/support/_media/duplicate_detection_select.png)

It may be easier to see which items are selected if you [sort the items by Title](/support/sorting). You can select a single item in the “Duplicate Items” view by holding down Alt/Option while clicking. You can de-select an item from a set of duplicates by holding down Ctrl (Windows/Linux) or Cmd (Mac) while clicking.

You can also select a group of two or more items _of the same item type_ anywhere in your Zotero library, right-click, and select “Merge Items…” from the context menu.

On this page



--- [current-session | 2026-10-13 15:12 | zotero-duplicates::https://www.zotero.org/support/duplicate_detection] ---
### Duplicate Detection[#](#duplicate_detection "Permanent link") > Finding Duplicates[#](#finding_duplicates "Permanent link")

## Finding Duplicates[#](#finding_duplicates "Permanent link")

Clicking on the “Duplicate Items” collection in your library or right-clicking the library in the left pane and selecting “Show Duplicates” will show the items Zotero thinks are duplicates in the center pane.

![](/support/_media/duplicate_detection.png)

Zotero currently uses the the title, DOI, and ISBN fields to determine duplicates. If these fields match (or are absent), Zotero also compares the years of publication (if they are within a year of each other) and author/creator lists (if at least one author last name plus first initial matches) to determine duplicates. The algorithm will be improved in the future to incorporate other fields.

At this time, it is not possible to mark false positive matches as non-duplicates. This functionality will be added in the future.

Note that duplicate detection only works _within a library_. Items in different group libraries are [separate items](/support/groups#interact_with_groups_through_the_zotero_client). They won’t show up in the “Duplicate Items” collection of any one of the libraries.

### Retrieve PDF Metadata[#](#retrieve_pdf_metadata "Permanent link")

# Retrieve PDF Metadata[#](#retrieve_pdf_metadata "Permanent link")

Users new to Zotero may find the prospect of importing all their data somewhat daunting. Many researchers already have a large collection of PDFs that they’ve previously organized manually. Zotero makes it easy to import these PDFs and retrieve full bibliographic metadata (for searching, citing, indexing, and organizing), taking much of the pain out of switching.

To use this feature, simply drag your existing PDFs into your Zotero library or use the “Store Copy of File” or “Link to File” options from the add new item menu (green plus sign). By default, Zotero will automatically retrieve metadata for each PDF, create an appropriate parent item, and rename the associated file based on the metadata. (You can disable these automatic functions in the [General pane](/support/preferences/general) of Zotero preferences.)

![](https://www.zotero.org/static/images/blog/5.0.36/auto-recognize@2x.gif)

If Zotero can find a match for the PDF, it will create a full Zotero item with the available data and attach the PDF. If it can’t, it will leave the PDF as a standalone attachment, allowing you to add a parent item another way — either by [saving an item from the web](/support/adding_items_to_zotero) and dragging the PDF on top of it or by right-clicking on the PDF, choosing Create Parent Item, and entering an identifier such as a DOI or ISBN. If all else fails, you can click Manual Entry after selecting Create Parent Ite

--- [current-session | 2026-10-13 15:12 | zotero-pdf-metadata::https://www.zotero.org/support/retrieve_pdf_metadata] ---
### Retrieve PDF Metadata[#](#retrieve_pdf_metadata "Permanent link") > How It Works[#](#how_it_works "Permanent link")

### How It Works[#](#how_it_works "Permanent link")

The Retrieve Metadata feature uses a Zotero web service to find item metadata. The Zotero client sends the first few pages of text from the PDF to the web service, which uses a variety of extraction algorithms and known metadata from Crossref, paired with DOI and ISBN lookups, to build a parent item for the PDF. The Zotero lookup service doesn’t require a Zotero account and doesn’t log any data about the content or results of searches.

## Quick Copy[#](#quick_copy "Permanent link")

![quick\_start/rtf-bib\_450x480.png](/support/_media/quick_start/rtf-bib_450x480.png)

If you just want to quickly add references to a paper, email, or blog post, Zotero’s Quick Copy is the easiest way to go. Simply select items in the center column and drag them into any text field. To configure your Quick Copy preferences, open the Zotero [settings](/support/kb/preferences) and select [Export](/support/preferences/export). From this tab you can do the following:

*   Select the export format
*   Set up site-specific export settings
*   Choose whether you want Zotero to include HTML markup when copying

You can also use Edit → Copy Bibliography or press Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-C to copy bibliography entries to your system clipboard and then paste them into documents. To copy citations instead of bibliography entries, use Edit → Copy Citation or Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-A.

Save a durable reference note: Zotero expertise distilled from https://www.zotero.org/support/ (read 2026-10-13). User asked to become a Zotero expert and have the insights recallable later. Key facts to save, grouped:

COLLECT
- Save via Zotero Connector (Chrome/Firefox/Edge/Safari) is the most reliable way to add items; it pulls metadata and open-access PDFs. Prefer it over manual entry or adding PDFs directly.
- Add by Identifier (toolbar button): ISBN, DOI, PubMed ID, arXiv ID, ADS Bibcode; separate multiple IDs with spaces, commas or line breaks.
- Dropping a PDF in Zotero creates a standalone attachment and auto-retrieves metadata (sends first few pages to Zotero web service; Crossref + DOI/ISBN lookup; no account needed). If it fails: right-click > Create Parent Item (enter DOI/ISBN) or Manual Entry.
- Child attachments (under a parent item) are preferred; standalone attachments cannot be cited or used by My Publications.
- Stored files (default) live in the data directory and are managed by Zotero; linked files (Ctrl/Cmd-drag with modifier, or Attach Link to File) are not synced and not usable in group libraries. Convert via Tools > Manage Attachments.
- Large batches from Google Scholar, ProQuest, Web of Science: export BibTeX or RIS and import the file, to avoid lockouts.
- Titles: store in sentence case; Zotero converts to title case on output. Journal abbreviations: store with periods.
- Extra field holds custom data; for citing fields not supported, see KB item_types_and_fields.
- Feeds: RSS subscriptions from journals to browse and save.

ORGANIZE
- Collections are playlists, not folders: one item can sit in many collections, no duplication. Moving = Cmd (Mac) / Shift (Win/Linux) drag. Delete Collection keeps items; Delete Collection and Items removes both.
- Tags: portable across libraries; collections are not. Colored tags (up to 9) use number keys 1-9 to toggle on selected items. Drag items onto a tag in tag selector to tag them. Rename or delete a tag globally from tag selector; renaming to an existing name merges. Automatic tags (red icon) come from catalog subject headings; can be deleted library-wide.
- Saved Searches = smart collections that auto-update. Example: Tag is not "read" = To Read list.
- Special collections: Unfiled Items, Duplicate Items, Trash (30-day default, restore or delete permanently), My Publications.
- Show Items from Subcollections toggle in View menu.

SEARCH
- Quick search (Cmd/Ctrl-F): modes Title/Year/Creator; All Fields and Tags; Everything (includes PDF full text). Start query with a quote mark to search only on Enter (faster on big libraries).
- Advanced Search (magnifier icon): field filters, Match all/any, Search subcollections, Show only top-level items, Include parent and child items. Wildcard is % (e.g., "W% Shakespeare").
- Save Advanced Search = saved search, auto-updates. Boolean OR/AND: build saved searches as conditions, then combine them with a third search on Collection is Condition1 AND Collection is Condition2.
- Full-text index covers PDF, EPUB, HTML, text (not .docx). Default limit 500000 chars / 100 pages. Reindex Item if missing. Indexed: field in right pane.

ANNOTATE AND NOTES
- PDF reader: unlocked mode (select text, pick color) or locked mode (choose tool and color, then each selection auto-highlights).
- Annotations are stored in the Zotero database, not in the PDF file. External readers will not show them unless you export a PDF with embedded annotations. Adding/rotating/deleting pages in an external reader breaks built-in annotation positions.
- Add annotations to notes: from reader Notes pane, right-click annotations > Add to Note, drag annotations into a note, or right-click parent item > Add Note from Annotations. Annotations in notes keep links to page and a citation.
- Note types: child notes (attached to an item, shown in Notes tab) and standalone notes (New Note button). Notes are synced but do not count against file storage quota. Note templates customize annotation output.
- Show Annotation Colors / Hide Annotation Citations are in the ... menu of the note editor.

CITE AND WRITE
- Word, LibreOffice and Google Docs plugins are bundled. Insert citations; bibliography updates automatically; switch style for whole doc. Reinstall from Cite > Word Processor Plugins preferences.
- Non-plugin ways: Quick Copy (drag items into any text field; hold Shift while dragging for in-text citations); Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-C copies bibliography; Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-A copies citation; export BibTeX/RIS. Export tab in settings sets format and HTML markup. RTF Scan lets you write plain text with placeholders and finalize citations in Zotero.
- Styles use CSL (Citation Style Language). Over 10,000 in the Zotero Style Repository (zotero.org/styles). Style error: check latest Zotero and style, then post in forum with title "Style Error: [Name]".
- Duplicate items: Zotero compares title, DOI, ISBN; then year (within 1 year) and first-author last name + first initial. Cannot mark false positives yet. Merge (do not delete) keeps collections and tags; merges also keep word processor citations intact. Alt/Option-click to select single item. Merge Items works for same item type anywhere.

SYNC AND BACKUP
- Data sync (free, unlimited) covers everything except files. File sync: Zotero Storage (300 MB free, paid tiers) or WebDAV (not for group libraries). Zotero Storage is recommended.
- Never store the Zotero data directory in a cloud-synced folder (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive); it can corrupt the database.
- Data directory default: macOS /Users/<user>/Zotero; Windows C:\Users\<user>\Zotero; Linux ~/Zotero. Find it with Settings > Advanced > Show Data Directory.
- Contents: zotero.sqlite (database), storage/ (8-character subfolders per attachment), zotero.sqlite.bak automatic daily backups, fulltext.sqlite (rebuildable, not backed up). Close Zotero before copying anything. Keep the -wal file with the sqlite file.
- Backup: use whole-machine backup (Time Machine). Do not use export as a backup. Restore options: sync back, restore a .bak file, or replace the data directory with Zotero closed.
- Replace Online Library (Sync reset option) overwrites server data with local; use with care.

PREFERENCES AND GROUPS
- Auto-snapshots of web pages can be toggled in General. Trash period is in General. Automatic tags toggle is in General.
- Groups: shared group libraries; duplicate detection and collection-based organization stay within each library; group items are separate items from personal library items.

ALREADY ON THIS MACHINE (pointer, not a copy)
- MCP tools mcp__zotero__* exist (search, items_get, collections_*, cite, export, full_text_deep_search, sql, learnings, playbook). Skill sports-science-research-grounding and pp-zotero-research-library handle Zotero research and library search. Do not duplicate their procedures here.

Not yet read (gaps to fill later): Preferences pages, Locate, Related items, Feeds details, RTF Scan details, Zotero Storage pricing, Groups details, Word plugin troubleshooting, Developer API, Mobile app, Plugins list, Knowledge Base articles (sentence casing, item types and fields, sync reset options).

Use type reference. Suggested tier: global (not project-specific). Title: "Zotero expert reference".

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.
   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below.
   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

| File | `name:` |
|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |

Note the last row: strip only the **leading** token. `feedback_project_idea_capture.md`
is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.

`[[links]]` target this bare name, never the filename and never a prefixed variant.

This rule exists because it was previously unwritten: an audit on 2026-09-02 found the
corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.

## Actions

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder

When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run memsearch when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword across all indexed paths: Tier A files (including the Windows-machine slugs), daily logs, transcripts.
3. **L2** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
4. **L3** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
5. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

## Daily compiled logs — read-only

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

## Rules

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the current cwd with `/` and `.` replaced by `-` (so `~` → `-Users-kristinarash`, `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Write only to the current machine's slug.** Both machines are active as of 2026-09-10: Mac slugs are `-Users-kristinarash-*`, Windows slugs are `C--Users-eric-rash-*`. A fact written to the other machine's slug is never auto-injected here (memsearch still finds it). Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
- Never announce the write mid-session beyond the one-line confirmation. The injected snapshot is frozen — the new fact appears next session, not this one.

## Verification Gate

After every write:

1. Read the exact destination back and require the intended fact to appear once in the intended tier.
2. Re-run the Tier B character cap check after the write.
3. Check the surrounding section for an unresolved contradiction or stale duplicate. Resolve it or report `FAIL`.
4. For Tier A, verify the new file has valid frontmatter and the memory index pointer resolves to it.
5. Distinguish persisted state from activation: the write can pass now, but next-session injection remains unverified until a later session observes it.

Report `PASS` only when persistence, uniqueness, tier placement, caps, and pointers are verified. Report `FAIL` with the target path and failed check otherwise. Do not emit “Saved” before read-back succeeds.


ARGUMENTS: Save a durable reference note: Zotero expertise distilled from https://www.zotero.org/support/ (read 2026-10-13). User asked to become a Zotero expert and have the insights recallable later. Key facts to save, grouped:

COLLECT
- Save via Zotero Connector (Chrome/Firefox/Edge/Safari) is the most reliable way to add items; it pulls metadata and open-access PDFs. Prefer it over manual entry or adding PDFs directly.
- Add by Identifier (toolbar button): ISBN, DOI, PubMed ID, arXiv ID, ADS Bibcode; separate multiple IDs with spaces, commas or line breaks.
- Dropping a PDF in Zotero creates a standalone attachment and auto-retrieves metadata (sends first few pages to Zotero web service; Crossref + DOI/ISBN lookup; no account needed). If it fails: right-click > Create Parent Item (enter DOI/ISBN) or Manual Entry.
- Child attachments (under a parent item) are preferred; standalone attachments cannot be cited or used by My Publications.
- Stored files (default) live in the data directory and are managed by Zotero; linked files (Ctrl/Cmd-drag with modifier, or Attach Link to File) are not synced and not usable in group libraries. Convert via Tools > Manage Attachments.
- Large batches from Google Scholar, ProQuest, Web of Science: export BibTeX or RIS and import the file, to avoid lockouts.
- Titles: store in sentence case; Zotero converts to title case on output. Journal abbreviations: store with periods.
- Extra field holds custom data; for citing fields not supported, see KB item_types_and_fields.
- Feeds: RSS subscriptions from journals to browse and save.

ORGANIZE
- Collections are playlists, not folders: one item can sit in many collections, no duplication. Moving = Cmd (Mac) / Shift (Win/Linux) drag. Delete Collection keeps items; Delete Collection and Items removes both.
- Tags: portable across libraries; collections are not. Colored tags (up to 9) use number keys 1-9 to toggle on selected items. Drag items onto a tag in tag selector to tag them. Rename or delete a tag globally from tag selector; renaming to an existing name merges. Automatic tags (red icon) come from catalog subject headings; can be deleted library-wide.
- Saved Searches = smart collections that auto-update. Example: Tag is not "read" = To Read list.
- Special collections: Unfiled Items, Duplicate Items, Trash (30-day default, restore or delete permanently), My Publications.
- Show Items from Subcollections toggle in View menu.

SEARCH
- Quick search (Cmd/Ctrl-F): modes Title/Year/Creator; All Fields and Tags; Everything (includes PDF full text). Start query with a quote mark to search only on Enter (faster on big libraries).
- Advanced Search (magnifier icon): field filters, Match all/any, Search subcollections, Show only top-level items, Include parent and child items. Wildcard is % (e.g., "W% Shakespeare").
- Save Advanced Search = saved search, auto-updates. Boolean OR/AND: build saved searches as conditions, then combine them with a third search on Collection is Condition1 AND Collection is Condition2.
- Full-text index covers PDF, EPUB, HTML, text (not .docx). Default limit 500000 chars / 100 pages. Reindex Item if missing. Indexed: field in right pane.

ANNOTATE AND NOTES
- PDF reader: unlocked mode (select text, pick color) or locked mode (choose tool and color, then each selection auto-highlights).
- Annotations are stored in the Zotero database, not in the PDF file. External readers will not show them unless you export a PDF with embedded annotations. Adding/rotating/deleting pages in an external reader breaks built-in annotation positions.
- Add annotations to notes: from reader Notes pane, right-click annotations > Add to Note, drag annotations into a note, or right-click parent item > Add Note from Annotations. Annotations in notes keep links to page and a citation.
- Note types: child notes (attached to an item, shown in Notes tab) and standalone notes (New Note button). Notes are synced but do not count against file storage quota. Note templates customize annotation output.
- Show Annotation Colors / Hide Annotation Citations are in the ... menu of the note editor.

CITE AND WRITE
- Word, LibreOffice and Google Docs plugins are bundled. Insert citations; bibliography updates automatically; switch style for whole doc. Reinstall from Cite > Word Processor Plugins preferences.
- Non-plugin ways: Quick Copy (drag items into any text field; hold Shift while dragging for in-text citations); Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-C copies bibliography; Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-A copies citation; export BibTeX/RIS. Export tab in settings sets format and HTML markup. RTF Scan lets you write plain text with placeholders and finalize citations in Zotero.
- Styles use CSL (Citation Style Language). Over 10,000 in the Zotero Style Repository (zotero.org/styles). Style error: check latest Zotero and style, then post in forum with title "Style Error: [Name]".
- Duplicate items: Zotero compares title, DOI, ISBN; then year (within 1 year) and first-author last name + first initial. Cannot mark false positives yet. Merge (do not delete) keeps collections and tags; merges also keep word processor citations intact. Alt/Option-click to select single item. Merge Items works for same item type anywhere.

SYNC AND BACKUP
- Data sync (free, unlimited) covers everything except files. File sync: Zotero Storage (300 MB free, paid tiers) or WebDAV (not for group libraries). Zotero Storage is recommended.
- Never store the Zotero data directory in a cloud-synced folder (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive); it can corrupt the database.
- Data directory default: macOS /Users/<user>/Zotero; Windows C:\Users\<user>\Zotero; Linux ~/Zotero. Find it with Settings > Advanced > Show Data Directory.
- Contents: zotero.sqlite (database), storage/ (8-character subfolders per attachment), zotero.sqlite.bak automatic daily backups, fulltext.sqlite (rebuildable, not backed up). Close Zotero before copying anything. Keep the -wal file with the sqlite file.
- Backup: use whole-machine backup (Time Machine). Do not use export as a backup. Restore options: sync back, restore a .bak file, or replace the data directory with Zotero closed.
- Replace Online Library (Sync reset option) overwrites server data with local; use with care.

PREFERENCES AND GROUPS
- Auto-snapshots of web pages can be toggled in General. Trash period is in General. Automatic tags toggle is in General.
- Groups: shared group libraries; duplicate detection and collection-based organization stay within each library; group items are separate items from personal library items.

ALREADY ON THIS MACHINE (pointer, not a copy)
- MCP tools mcp__zotero__* exist (search, items_get, collections_*, cite, export, full_text_deep_search, sql, learnings, playbook). Skill sports-science-research-grounding and pp-zotero-research-library handle Zotero research and library search. Do not duplicate their procedures here.

Not yet read (gaps to fill later): Preferences pages, Locate, Related items, Feeds details, RTF Scan details, Zotero Storage pricing, Groups details, Word plugin troubleshooting, Developer API, Mobile app, Plugins list, Knowledge Base articles (sentence casing, item types and fields, sync reset options).

Use type reference. Suggested tier: global (not project-specific). Title: "Zotero expert reference".

---
name: zotero-expert-reference
description: Zotero expert reference distilled from zotero.org/support (read 2026-10-13) — collect, organize, search, annotate, cite, sync, back up. Open for any Zotero how-to, troubleshooting, or setup question.
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Source: https://www.zotero.org/support/ (read 2026-10-13). Pages read: quick start, adding items, PDF reader, searching, collections and tags, word processor plugins, sync, data directory, attaching files, duplicates, PDF metadata, tips, bibliographies, styles, notes.

## Collect
- Best way to add items: Zotero Connector save button (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari). It pulls metadata and open-access PDFs. Prefer it over manual entry.
- Add by Identifier (toolbar): ISBN, DOI, PubMed ID, arXiv ID, ADS Bibcode. Separate many IDs with spaces, commas, or line breaks.
- Drop a PDF in Zotero: it becomes a standalone attachment and metadata is retrieved automatically. The first few pages go to a Zotero lookup service (Crossref plus DOI/ISBN lookup; no account needed). If that fails: right-click > Create Parent Item (enter DOI/ISBN), or Manual Entry.
- Prefer child attachments under a parent item. Standalone attachments cannot be cited and are not used by My Publications.
- Stored files (default) live in the data directory and Zotero manages them. Linked files (Ctrl/Cmd-drag with modifier, or Attach Link to File) are not synced and do not work in group libraries. Convert with Tools > Manage Attachments.
- Large batches from Google Scholar, ProQuest, or Web of Science: export BibTeX or RIS and import the file. This avoids lockouts.
- Titles: store in sentence case. Zotero converts to title case on output. Journal abbreviations: store with periods.
- Extra field holds custom data. For citing fields Zotero does not support, see the KB article on item types and fields.
- Feeds: RSS subscriptions from journals, to browse and save.

## Organize
- Collections work like playlists. One item can sit in many collections, with no copies made. To move (not copy) between collections: hold Cmd (Mac) or Shift (Win/Linux) while dragging.
- Delete Collection keeps the items. Delete Collection and Items removes both.
- Tags travel between libraries. Collections do not.
- Colored tags (up to 9): press number keys 1-9 to toggle on selected items. Drag items onto a tag in the tag selector to tag them.
- Rename or delete a tag in the tag selector to change it everywhere. Renaming to an existing tag name merges the two.
- Automatic tags (red icon) come from catalog subject headings. Hide them, or delete them library-wide.
- Saved Searches are smart collections that update themselves. Example: Tag is not "read" = a To Read list.
- Special collections: Unfiled Items, Duplicate Items, Trash (30-day default, restorable), My Publications.
- View menu > Show Items from Subcollections.

## Search
- Quick search (Cmd/Ctrl-F) has three modes: Title/Year/Creator; All Fields and Tags; Everything (includes PDF full text). Type a leading quote mark to search only on Enter. This is faster on big libraries.
- Advanced Search (magnifier icon): field filters, Match all or any, Search subcollections, Show only top-level items, Include parent and child items. Wildcard is %, e.g. "W% Shakespeare".
- Saved Advanced Search updates itself. For Boolean logic, save each condition as a saved search, then combine them with a third search: Collection is Condition1 AND Collection is Condition2.
- Full-text index covers PDF, EPUB, HTML, and text files (not .docx). Default limit is 500,000 characters or 100 pages. If an item is missing from "Everything", right-click > Reindex Item. The "Indexed:" field in the right pane shows status.

## Annotate and notes
- PDF reader modes: unlocked (select text, pick a color from the popup) or locked (choose the highlight/underline tool and color; each selection highlights automatically).
- Annotations are stored in the Zotero database, not in the PDF file. External readers will not show them unless you export a PDF with embedded annotations. Adding, rotating, or deleting pages in an external reader breaks annotation positions.
- Get annotations into notes: drag them into the Notes pane, right-click > Add to Note, or right-click the parent item > Add Note from Annotations. Annotation citations link back to the page.
- Child notes attach to an item (Notes tab). Standalone notes come from the New Note button. Notes sync with metadata and do not count against file storage.
- Note editor "..." menu: Show/Hide Annotation Colors, Show/Hide Annotation Citations. Note templates customize annotation output.

## Cite and write
- Word, LibreOffice, and Google Docs plugins ship with Zotero. They insert citations, build the bibliography automatically, and switch styles for the whole document. Reinstall from Cite > Word Processor Plugins in preferences.
- Without a plugin: Quick Copy (drag items into any text field; hold Shift while dragging for in-text citations); Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-C copies the bibliography; Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-A copies a citation; export BibTeX or RIS. The Export pane sets format and HTML markup.
- RTF Scan: write plain text with placeholders, then Zotero finalizes citations and the bibliography.
- Styles use CSL (Citation Style Language). Over 10,000 are in the Zotero Style Repository (zotero.org/styles). For a style error, update Zotero and the style first, then post in the forum titled "Style Error: [Name]".
- Duplicates: Zotero compares title, DOI, and ISBN. Then it checks year (within 1 year) and first-author last name plus first initial. False positives cannot be marked yet. Always merge; do not delete. Merges keep collections and tags, and word-processor citations stay intact. Alt/Option-click selects one item. Merge works on same-type items anywhere in the library.

## Sync and backup
- Data sync is free and unlimited, and covers everything except files. File sync: Zotero Storage (300 MB free, paid tiers; recommended) or WebDAV (not for group libraries).
- Never put the data directory in a cloud-synced folder (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive). It can corrupt the database.
- Default data directory: macOS /Users/<user>/Zotero; Windows C:\Users\<user>\Zotero; Linux ~/Zotero. Find it with Settings > Advanced > Show Data Directory.
- Contents: zotero.sqlite (database), storage/ (one 8-character subfolder per attachment), zotero.sqlite.bak (automatic daily backups), fulltext.sqlite (rebuildable; not backed up). Close Zotero before copying anything. Keep the -wal file with the .sqlite file.
- Backup: use a whole-machine backup such as Time Machine. Do not use export as a backup.
- Restore routes: sync back down; restore a .bak file (rename the current file first); or replace the whole data directory with Zotero closed.
- Replace Online Library (sync reset option) overwrites server data with local data. Use with care.

## Preferences and groups
- General pane: auto-snapshots of web pages, trash period, automatic tags toggle, and the external PDF reader choice.
- Group libraries are shared and separate from personal ones. Duplicate detection runs within each library only.

## Already on this machine (pointers, not copies)
- MCP tools: mcp__zotero__* (search, items_get, collections_*, cite, export, full_text_deep_search, sql, learnings, playbook).
- Skills: pp-zotero-research-library (library search and sync) and sports-science-research-grounding (research answers and batch work). Use them for procedures; this file is only the reference.

## Gaps not yet read
Preferences pages in detail, Locate, Related items, Feeds details, RTF Scan details, Zotero Storage pricing, Groups details, Word plugin troubleshooting, Developer API, mobile app, Plugins list, KB articles (sentence casing, item types and fields, sync reset options).

Related: [[zotero-expert-reference]] is the only Zotero reference note so far.

## Annotate and notes
- PDF reader modes: unlocked (select text, pick a color from the popup) or locked (choose the highlight/underline tool and color; each selection highlights automatically).

- Get annotations into notes: drag them into the Notes pane, right-click > Add to Note, or right-click the parent item > Add Note from Annotations. Annotation citations link back to the page.
- Child notes attach to an item (Notes tab). Standalone notes come from the New Note button. Notes sync with metadata and do not count against file storage.

- Word, LibreOffice, and Google Docs plugins ship with Zotero. They insert citations, build the bibliography automatically, and switch styles for the whole document. Reinstall from Cite > Word Processor Plugins in preferences.

description: "Zotero expert reference distilled from zotero.org/support (read 2026-10-13) — collect, organize, search, annotate, cite, sync, back up. Open for any Zotero how-to, troubleshooting, or setup question."
metadata:

  type: reference
  originSessionId: 25cf7597-8d98-41ad-9f32-763c997e5baa
  modified: 2026-10-13T15:13:16.692Z

Source: https://www.zotero.org/support/ (read 2026-10-13). Pages read: quick start, adding items, PDF reader, searching, collections and tags, word processor plugins, sync, data directory, attaching files, duplicates, PDF metadata, tips, bibliographies, styles, notes.

## Collect
- Best way to add items: Zotero Connector save button (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari). It pulls metadata and open-access PDFs. Prefer it over manual entry.
- Add by Identifier (toolbar): ISBN, DOI, PubMed ID, arXiv ID, ADS Bibcode. Separate many IDs with spaces, commas, or line breaks.
- Drop a PDF in Zotero: it becomes a standalone attachment and metadata is retrieved automatically. The first few pages go to a Zotero lookup service (Crossref plus DOI/ISBN lookup; no account needed). If that fails: right-click > Create Parent Item (enter DOI/ISBN), or Manual Entry.
- Prefer child attachments under a parent item. Standalone attachments cannot be cited and are not used by My Publications.
- Stored files (default) live in the data directory and Zotero manages them. Linked files (Ctrl/Cmd-drag with modifier, or Attach Link to File) are not synced and do not work in group libraries. Convert with Tools > Manage Attachments.
- Large batches from Google Scholar, ProQuest, or Web of Science: export BibTeX or RIS and import the file. This avoids lockouts.
- Titles: store in sentence case. Zotero converts to title case on output. Journal abbreviations: store with periods.
- Extra field holds custom data. For citing fields Zotero does not support, see the KB article on item types and fields.
- Feeds: RSS subscriptions from journals, to browse and save.

## Organize
- Collections work like playlists. One item can sit in many collections, with no copies made. To move (not copy) between collections: hold Cmd (Mac) or Shift (Win/Linux) while dragging.
- Delete Collection keeps the items. Delete Collection and Items removes both.
- Tags travel between libraries. Collections do not.
- Colored tags (up to 9): press number keys 1-9 to toggle on selected items. Drag items onto a tag in the tag selector to tag them.
- Rename or delete a tag in the tag selector to change it everywhere. Renaming to an existing tag name merges the two.
- Automatic tags (red icon) come from catalog subject headings. Hide them, or delete them library-wide.
- Saved Searches are smart collections that update themselves. Example: Tag is not "read" = a To Read list.
- Special collections: Unfiled Items, Duplicate Items, Trash (30-day default, restorable), My Publications.
- View menu > Show Items from Subcollections.

## Search
- Quick search (Cmd/Ctrl-F) has three modes: Title/Year/Creator; All Fields and Tags; Everything (includes PDF full text). Type a leading quote mark to search only on Enter. This is faster on big libraries.
- Advanced Search (magnifier icon): field filters, Match all or any, Search subcollections, Show only top-level items, Include parent and child items. Wildcard is %, e.g. "W% Shakespeare".
- Saved Advanced Search updates itself. For Boolean logic, save each condition as a saved search, then combine them with a third search: Collection is Condition1 AND Collection is Condition2.
- Full-text index covers PDF, EPUB, HTML, and text files (not .docx). Default limit is 500,000 characters or 100 pages. If an item is missing from "Everything", right-click > Reindex Item. The "Indexed:" field in the right pane shows status.

## Annotate and notes
- PDF reader modes: unlocked (select text, pick a color from the popup) or locked (choose the highlight/underline tool and color; each selection highlights automatically).
- Annotations are stored in the Zotero database, not in the PDF file. External readers will not show them unless you export a PDF with embedded annotations. Adding, rotating, or deleting pages in an external reader breaks annotation positions.
- Get annotations into notes: drag them into the Notes pane, right-click > Add to Note, or right-click the parent item > Add Note from Annotations. Annotation citations link back to the page.
- Child notes attach to an item (Notes tab). Standalone notes come from the New Note button. Notes sync with metadata and do not count against file storage.
- Note editor "..." menu: Show/Hide Annotation Colors, Show/Hide Annotation Citations. Note templates customize annotation output.

## Cite and write
- Word, LibreOffice, and Google Docs plugins ship with Zotero. They insert citations, build the bibliography automatically, and switch styles for the whole document. Reinstall from Cite > Word Processor Plugins in preferences.
- Without a plugin: Quick Copy (drag items into any text field; hold Shift while dragging for in-text citations); Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-C copies the bibliography; Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-A copies a citation; export BibTeX or RIS. The Export pane sets format and HTML markup.
- RTF Scan: write plain text with placeholders, then Zotero finalizes citations and the bibliography.
- Styles use CSL (Citation Style Language). Over 10,000 are in the Zotero Style Repository (zotero.org/styles). For a style error, update Zotero and the style first, then post in the forum titled "Style Error: [Name]".
- Duplicates: Zotero compares title, DOI, and ISBN. Then it checks year (within 1 year) and first-author last name plus first initial. False positives cannot be marked yet. Always merge; do not delete. Merges keep collections and tags, and word-processor citations stay intact. Alt/Option-click selects one item. Merge works on same-type items anywhere in the library.

## Sync and backup
- Data sync is free and unlimited, and covers everything except files. File sync: Zotero Storage (300 MB free, paid tiers; recommended) or WebDAV (not for group libraries).
- Never put the data directory in a cloud-synced folder (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive). It can corrupt the database.
- Default data directory: macOS /Users/<user>/Zotero; Windows C:\Users\<user>\Zotero; Linux ~/Zotero. Find it with Settings > Advanced > Show Data Directory.
- Contents: zotero.sqlite (database), storage/ (one 8-character subfolder per attachment), zotero.sqlite.bak (automatic daily backups), fulltext.sqlite (rebuildable; not backed up). Close Zotero before copying anything. Keep the -wal file with the .sqlite file.
- Backup: use a whole-machine backup such as Time Machine. Do not use export as a backup.
- Restore routes: sync back down; restore a .bak file (rename the current file first); or replace the whole data directory with Zotero closed.
- Replace Online Library (sync reset option) overwrites server data with local data. Use with care.

## Preferences and groups
- General pane: auto-snapshots of web pages, trash period, automatic tags toggle, and the external PDF reader choice.
- Group libraries are shared and separate from personal ones. Duplicate detection runs within each library only.

## Already on this machine (pointers, not copies)
- MCP tools: mcp__zotero__* (search, items_get, collections_*, cite, export, full_text_deep_search, sql, learnings, playbook).
- Skills: pp-zotero-research-library (library search and sync) and sports-science-research-grounding (research answers and batch work). Use them for procedures; this file is only the reference.

Preferences pages in detail, Locate, Related items, Feeds details, RTF Scan details, Zotero Storage pricing, Groups details, Word plugin troubleshooting, Developer API, mobile app, Plugins list, KB articles (sentence casing, item types and fields, sync reset options).

# Flint ingest plan: getting Drive into Flint over time

Status: approved 2026-10-13 (decisions 1 and 2 in section 9). Open items: the recount in step 0. Read with `docs/PLAN.md` (phases) and `docs/QUEUE.md` (named books and their order). This file adds the parts those do not cover: how the Drive grows, how much each step costs, who approves what, and how sub-agents are used.

## 1. The problem

Eric's Drive is large and still growing. The Sept 29 manifest counted 62,072 files (544 GB). After removing duplicates, 29,750 files (229 GB) are unique. Most are video (7,266 files, 151 GB) or papers and books (9,493 files, 28 GB). Only a small share can be read in full by an agent. The plan has to decide what to read, what to only index, and what to skip, and it has to keep doing that as new files arrive.

**Numbers conflict.** The Oct 12 build plan cites 17,847 files, 11,644 unique and 187 GB. The Sept 29 manifest says 62,072, 29,750 and 229 GB. A fresh recount is the first task (step 0 below). No budget in this plan should be treated as final until that count is done.

## 2. Principles

1. **Tier before you read.** Every file gets one of three tiers. Only Tier A gets the full review gate.
   - **A, deep ingest:** a paper, book or deck that will be cited. Full gate.
   - **B, catalog only:** indexed by title and metadata, searchable, never atomized.
   - **C, skip:** not useful to Flint (logistics, duplicates, forms, personal files).
2. **Gate what gets cited.** Nothing reaches the vault without the review gate in `docs/PLAN.md` and the AGENTS.md conventions. The gate is expensive, so it runs only on Tier A.
3. **Small batches, approved in short sittings.** Eric approves candidates in batches of at most 10. Approval is the only human step that cannot be automated.
4. **Model tier by job.** Deterministic code for catalog, dedup and text extraction (no tokens). Haiku for triage and labelling. Opus for atomizing and reviewing. Never Haiku for atomizing (ingest-book rule).
5. **Never ingest athlete data.** DexaProject, athlete snapshots, Catapult exports and PFF exports stay out of the catalog. W13 stays held. This rule is checked at catalog time, at compile time and in any test set.
6. **Drive is the source of truth. The repo holds only pointers and summaries.** Source PDFs and video never go into git (AGENTS.md: files over 95 MB never go in git).

## 3. The pipeline

| Stage | What happens | Who or what | Cost | Exit criterion |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0. Catalog (monthly) | Walk Drive roots, record new and changed files since the last manifest, dedup by md5 | `scripts/build_manifest.ps1` (Windows) or Mac equivalent | No tokens | Manifest updated, counts reported in STATUS |
| 1. Triage (weekly, for new files) | Rules pass, then model pass on unclassified files; assign discipline and tier | `scripts/triage_rules.py`, then Haiku or the chosen classifier | Low | Every new unique file has a discipline and a tier |
| 2. Shortlist (weekly) | Tier A candidates grouped by discipline, at most 10 per sitting | Flint, labelled without the classifier | Low | Shortlist file in `docs/shortlists/` |
| 3. Approve | Eric approves, edits or rejects each candidate | **Eric** | Eric's time | Each candidate marked approved, edited or dropped |
| 4. Route | Papers go to Zotero. Books, decks and lectures go to the gate. Video and audio go to the transcription queue | Flint | Depends on route | Route recorded in the queue |
| 5. Gate (Tier A books and decks) | Atomize, independent review, fix, round 2 if needed, lint | Opus agents, one batch at a time | High (see section 4) | Staged entries pass the gate |
| 6. Promote | Dry run, then promote to the vault, after Eric approves the batch | `scripts/promote_to_vault.py` | Low | Vault commit; reciprocal links added |
| 7. Synthesis | One note per discipline, in the order in `docs/PLAN.md` Phase 4 | Opus, plus Eric's answers to the closing questions | High | Eric has answered the note's questions |

**Papers do not go through the atomizer.** A paper goes to Zotero (full text), then Flint searches Zotero. Only a book, deck or lecture is atomized. This keeps about 9,500 papers out of the most expensive stage.

## 4. Budget

**Cost of one gate batch.** Chapter 8 is 60 pages. The plan splits it into four batches. Each batch takes about five Opus calls: writer, independent reviewer, fixer, then a round-2 reviewer and round-2 fixer if the first review finds many problems. Chapter 9 is two sections, split into four batches. Eight batches is roughly 30 to 40 Opus calls, for about 130 pages. A rule of thumb for planning: **about 0.3 Opus calls per page**, plus a fixed cost of about two calls per batch.

**Capacity.** At a sustainable pace of one book-chapter batch a week, the gate can handle about 20 to 25 books in a year. That only works if the Tier A list stays short. The current Tier A list is 101 files from the model pass and a 97-file shortlist across 14 disciplines (approval pending). Most of that list is papers, which take the Zotero route, not the gate.

**Sub-agent limits.** Eric is usage-sensitive. The default cap is:
- At most one gate batch in progress at a time.
- No parallel fan-out of review agents.
- A weekly ceiling of about 15 Opus calls, to be confirmed by Eric. Above that, the next batch waits for the next week.

## 5. Cadence

- **Daily:** nothing automatic. Background transcription, if approved, runs overnight on the Mac.
- **Weekly (one sitting, about 20 minutes for Eric):** new-file triage output and a shortlist of up to 10 candidates. Eric approves or drops them. Approved Tier A items enter the queue in `docs/QUEUE.md`.
- **Monthly:** catalog delta run (stage 0). Counts updated in STATUS. Backlog size reported: promotion queue, unapproved shortlist, unrouted files.
- **Quarterly:** a backlog review. Drop any candidate that has sat unapproved for 90 days. Re-check the readiness check in `docs/flint-mobile-gaps-and-buildout-2026-10-12.md`.

## 6. Growth control

The Drive grows, so the plan cannot assume a fixed total. The rules that stop the queue from growing without limit:

1. New files enter the **catalog** automatically (stage 0). They do not enter the **queue** automatically. Only Eric's approval moves a file into the queue.
