# Zotero — Printing Press CLI

## Prerequisites: Install the CLI

This skill drives the `zotero-research-library-pp-cli` binary. **You must verify the CLI is installed before invoking any command from this skill.** If it is missing, install it first:

1. Install via the Printing Press installer. It defaults binaries to `$HOME/.local/bin` on macOS/Linux and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\PrintingPress\bin` on Windows:
   ```bash
   npx -y @mvanhorn/printing-press-library install zotero-research-library --cli-only
   ```
2. Verify: `zotero-research-library-pp-cli --version`
3. Ensure the reported install directory is on `$PATH` for the agent/runtime that will invoke this skill.

If the `npx` install fails (no Node, offline, etc.), fall back to a direct Go install (requires Go 1.26.5 or newer). This installs into `$GOPATH/bin` (default `$HOME/go/bin`), so add that directory to `$PATH` instead:

```bash
go install github.com/mvanhorn/printing-press-library/library/productivity/zotero-research-library/cmd/zotero-research-library-pp-cli@latest
```

If `--version` reports "command not found" after install, the runtime cannot see the binary directory on `$PATH`. Do not proceed with skill commands until verification succeeds.

zotero-research-library-pp-cli mirrors your library into a local SQLite cache using the API's version cursors, then answers research-grounding questions offline: ranked full-text search with snippets, collection trees, recent-additions triage, and Better BibTeX citekey lookups. What the Web API meters at 100 items a page, your cache answers in milliseconds.

## When to Use This CLI

Use this CLI whenever a task needs the user's own research library: grounding answers in their curated corpus, finding citations, browsing collections, or exporting BibTeX. It is the substrate for research-grounding workflows — search the local cache first, fall back to live API or open web only when the cache misses.

## Anti-triggers

Do not use this CLI for:
- Do not use this CLI to create, modify, or delete items in Zotero — it is read-only against the API
- Do not use it for PDF download or attachment file retrieval; it indexes extracted text only
- Do not use it for open-web literature search — it covers the user's own library

## Unique Capabilities

These capabilities aren't available in any other tool for this API.

### Research grounding that compounds
- **`ground`** — Ranked full-text search over your synced library — title, abstract, creators, tags, and attachment full text — answered offline in under a second, with snippets and citation-ready metadata.

  _Reach for this when asked what the user's own library says about a topic._

  ```bash
  zotero-research-library-pp-cli ground "hamstring injury prevention" --limit 10 --agent
  ```
- **`items recent`** — What landed in the library recently, sorted by dateAdded from the local cache, with a --days cutoff and pipeable keys.

  _Use for weekly triage of new additions._

  ```bash
  zotero-research-library-pp-cli items recent --days 7 --agent
  ```
- **`collections tree`** — Renders the full collection hierarchy with per-node item counts in one command — a shape the flat API cannot return in one call.

42:**Capacity.** At a sustainable pace of one book-chapter batch a week, the gate can handle about 20 to 25 books in a year. That only works if the Tier A list stays short. The current Tier A list is 101 files from the model pass and a 97-file shortlist across 14 disciplines (approval pending). Most of that list is papers, which take the Zotero route, not the gate.
70:4. **Route the shortlist:** papers to Zotero, books and decks to the gate, video to the transcription queue.

# Zotero — Printing Press CLI

## Prerequisites: Install the CLI

This skill drives the `zotero-research-library-pp-cli` binary. **You must verify the CLI is installed before invoking any command from this skill.** If it is missing, install it first:

1. Install via the Printing Press installer. It defaults binaries to `$HOME/.local/bin` on macOS/Linux and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\PrintingPress\bin` on Windows:
   ```bash
   npx -y @mvanhorn/printing-press-library install zotero-research-library --cli-only
   ```
2. Verify: `zotero-research-library-pp-cli --version`
3. Ensure the reported install directory is on `$PATH` for the agent/runtime that will invoke this skill.

If the `npx` install fails (no Node, offline, etc.), fall back to a direct Go install (requires Go 1.26.5 or newer). This installs into `$GOPATH/bin` (default `$HOME/go/bin`), so add that directory to `$PATH` instead:

```bash
go install github.com/mvanhorn/printing-press-library/library/productivity/zotero-research-library/cmd/zotero-research-library-pp-cli@latest
```

If `--version` reports "command not found" after install, the runtime cannot see the binary directory on `$PATH`. Do not proceed with skill commands until verification succeeds.

zotero-research-library-pp-cli mirrors your library into a local SQLite cache using the API's version cursors, then answers research-grounding questions offline: ranked full-text search with snippets, collection trees, recent-additions triage, and Better BibTeX citekey lookups. What the Web API meters at 100 items a page, your cache answers in milliseconds.

## When to Use This CLI

Use this CLI whenever a task needs the user's own research library: grounding answers in their curated corpus, finding citations, browsing collections, or exporting BibTeX. It is the substrate for research-grounding workflows — search the local cache first, fall back to live API or open web only when the cache misses.

## Anti-triggers

Do not use this CLI for:
- Do not use this CLI to create, modify, or delete items in Zotero — it is read-only against the API
- Do not use it for PDF download or attachment file retrieval; it indexes extracted text only
- Do not use it for open-web literature search — it covers the user's own library

## Unique Capabilities

These capabilities aren't available in any other tool for this API.

### Research grounding that compounds
- **`ground`** — Ranked full-text search over your synced library — title, abstract, creators, tags, and attachment full text — answered offline in under a second, with snippets and citation-ready metadata.

  _Reach for this when asked what the user's own library says about a topic._

  ```bash
  zotero-research-library-pp-cli ground "hamstring injury prevention" --limit 10 --agent
  ```
- **`items recent`** — What landed in the library recently, sorted by dateAdded from the local cache, with a --days cutoff and pipeable keys.

  _Use for weekly triage of new additions._

  ```bash
  zotero-research-library-pp-cli items recent --days 7 --agent
  ```
- **`collections tree`** — Renders the full collection hierarchy with per-node item counts in one command — a shape the flat API cannot return in one call.

### Advanced[#](#advanced "Permanent link") > Files and Folders[#](#files_and_folders "Permanent link") > Linked Attachment Base Directory[#](#linked_attachment_base_directory "Permanent link")

#### Linked Attachment Base Directory[#](#linked_attachment_base_directory "Permanent link")

_If you store attached files in Zotero — the default — this setting does not affect you. It only applies to_ linked _files._

This setting allows you to access [linked files](/support/attaching_files#stored_files_and_linked_files) on multiple computers even when they’re stored in different locations on each computer. You should set the base directory to the folder on each computer under which you store linked files. For example, if the folder with your linked files is at `/Users/Sarah/Dropbox/PDFs` on your laptop and at `C:\Users\Sarah\Dropbox\PDFs` on your work computer, set those paths as the base directory on each respective machine. If you add a linked file within the base directory, Zotero stores a relative path to that base directory rather than an absolute path.

Note that this setting does not control where files are stored — only whether linked files within the specified folder are referenced by absolute or relative paths. If you’re using a plugin to help with a linked-file workflow, you should configure it to store linked files within the base directory you’ve configured.

Note that linked files are an advanced configuration, and we’re not able to help troubleshoot problems with specific setups. We recommend that most people use stored files instead.

When viewing a feed, unread items will be shown in bold text, while read items are shown in regular text. When you select an item in the feed, you can mark it as read or unread by clicking the “Mark As Unread/Read” button or pressing the `` ` `` key. Save the item to your Zotero library by clicking on the “Save to My Library” button or pressing Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-S. You can save a feed item to a group library by clicking the dropdown arrow on the right side of the “Save to My Library” button and choosing the group library.

_Note, the read/unread state of items is not synced across computers when using Zotero sync._

## Interact With Groups Through the Zotero Client[#](#interact_with_groups_through_the_zotero_client "Permanent link")

If you have [enabled data syncing](/support/sync#data_syncing) and are a member of a group with an enabled library, the group library will appear in Zotero’s left pane. ### Quick Copy[#](#quick_copy "Permanent link")

Quick Copy allows you to quickly export items in the specified format. You can set your Quick Copy **Default Format** to either a citation style, such as Chicago Manual of Style (note), or a bibliographic export format, such as BibLaTeX or Zotero RDF. Press Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-C to copy the full reference to the clipboard. You can also drag the item to any text box in another program. If you set your default format to a citation style, press Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-A or hold down Shfit before dragging to copy the in-text ciation or footnote.

Besides setting the default Quick Copy format, you can also change these Quick Copy settings:

*   **Language:** What languages should be used for Quick Copy bibliographies and citations?
*   **Copy as HTML:** Quick Copy citations as regular text (default, generally recommended) or HTML (useful for pasting in web pages).
*   **Site-Specific Settings:** These settings can change the default Quick Copy format when a specific website is open in your web browswer with the [Zotero Connector plugin](/download) installed. For example, you can set the default export style to Wikipedia Citation Templates when copying references to insert into Wikipedia articles. ### Creating Bibliographies[#](#creating_bibliographies "Permanent link") > Quick Copy[#](#quick_copy "Permanent link")

## Quick Copy[#](#quick_copy "Permanent link")

![quick\_start/rtf-bib\_450x480.png](/support/_media/quick_start/rtf-bib_450x480.png)

If you just want to quickly add references to a paper, email, or blog post, Zotero’s Quick Copy is the easiest way to go. Simply select items in the center column and drag them into any text field. Zotero will automatically create a formatted bibliography for you. To copy citations instead of references, hold down Shift at the start of the drag.

To configure your Quick Copy preferences, open the Zotero [settings](/support/kb/preferences) and select [Export](/support/preferences/export). From this tab you can do the following:

*   Select the export format
*   Set up site-specific export settings
*   Choose whether you want Zotero to include HTML markup when copying

You can also use Edit → Copy Bibliography or press Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-C to copy bibliography entries to your system clipboard and then paste them into documents. To copy citations instead of bibliography entries, use Edit → Copy Citation or Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-A.

In addition to bibliographic output, Quick Copy also supports export formats such as BibTeX and RIS.

#### Data Syncing[#](#data_syncing "Permanent link")

*   **Unlink Account…:** Disconnect the client from your Zotero account. This will prevent syncing. You will be given an option to remove the local Zotero data or keep it. If you later link this Zotero client with another username, the local library will be replaced with the new username’s library from [zotero.org](/).
*   **Choose Libraries…:** This option lets you choose which of the [Group libraries](/support/groups) you are a member of to sync automatically with the Zotero servers. If you uncheck a library that is present in your local Zotero client, you can still manually sync the library by right-clicking on it in the left Zotero pane and choosing “Sync Library”. It is not currently possible to remove an unsynced library from the local Zotero client.
*   **Sync automatically:** When check, Zotero will start a sync every time you make a change to your library. You can manually start a sync by clicking the sync button (circular green arrow) in the upper-right corner of the Zotero window.
*   **Sync full-text content:** When checked, Zotero will sync the extracted text contents of your PDFs and other files, allowing you to perform searches across devices regardless of whether files have been downloaded to a particular device. This also allows for full-text searches in the [web library](/mylibrary).

See [Data Syncing](/support/sync#data_syncing) for more information.

An active community of Zotero users has developed plugins to provide enhancements, new features, and interfaces with other programs.

We don’t currently provide a list of available plugins, but most plugins are announced and discussed in the [Zotero Forums](/forum). An official plugin directory is planned.

Note: [Word processor plugins](/support/word_processor_integration) for Word, LibreOffice, and Google Docs are bundled with Zotero. Extensions for Firefox, Chrome, and Edge are available from the [download page](/download/).

## linked attachment base directory

--- [current-session | 2026-10-13 15:15 | zotero-prefs-advanced::https://www.zotero.org/support/preferences/advanced] ---
### Advanced[#](#advanced "Permanent link") > Files and Folders[#](#files_and_folders "Permanent link") > Linked Attachment Base Directory[#](#linked_attachment_base_directory "Permanent link")

#### Linked Attachment Base Directory[#](#linked_attachment_base_directory "Permanent link")

_If you store attached files in Zotero — the default — this setting does not affect you. It only applies to_ linked _files._

This setting allows you to access [linked files](/support/attaching_files#stored_files_and_linked_files) on multiple computers even when they’re stored in different locations on each computer. You should set the base directory to the folder on each computer under which you store linked files. For example, if the folder with your linked files is at `/Users/Sarah/Dropbox/PDFs` on your laptop and at `C:\Users\Sarah\Dropbox\PDFs` on your work computer, set those paths as the base directory on each respective machine. If you add a linked file within the base directory, Zotero stores a relative path to that base directory rather than an absolute path.

Note that this setting does not control where files are stored — only whether linked files within the specified folder are referenced by absolute or relative paths. If you’re using a plugin to help with a linked-file workflow, you should configure it to store linked files within the base directory you’ve configured.

Note that linked files are an advanced configuration, and we’re not able to help troubleshoot problems with specific setups. We recommend that most people use stored files instead.

### Reading Feeds[#](#reading_feeds "Permanent link")

![](/support/_media/feed_window.png)

Feeds you have subscribed to will appear at the bottom of the left pane of the Zotero window, below My Library and your Group Libraries and above the tag selector. Click on a feed to view currently available items in the feed. Right-click on a feed to manually refresh it, mark all items in the feed as read, modify feed settings, or unsubscribe from the feed.

When viewing a feed, unread items will be shown in bold text, while read items are shown in regular text. When you select an item in the feed, you can mark it as read or unread by clicking the “Mark As Unread/Read” button or pressing the `` ` `` key. Save the item to your Zotero library by clicking on the “Save to My Library” button or pressing Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-S. You can save a feed item to a group library by clicking the dropdown arrow on the right side of the “Save to My Library” button and choosing the group library.

_Note, the read/unread state of items is not synced across computers when using Zotero sync._

## Shortcuts[#](#shortcuts "Permanent link")

![preferences\_advanced\_shortcuts.png](/support/_media/preferences_advanced_shortcuts.png)

This tab allows you to change Zotero’s default keyboard shortcuts.

*   **Create a New Item:** Create a new blank item in the current collection.
*   **Create a New Note:** Create a new standalone note in the current collection.
*   **Focus Libraries Pane:** Sets the focus in Zotero to left (libraries, collections, and feeds) pane.
*   **Quick Search:** Sets the focus to the [Quick search](/support/preferences/searching) box. `Ctrl/Cmd`\-`F` will also focus the Quick search box.
*   **Copy Selected Item Citations to Clipboard:** Copies an inline citation for the selected item(s) to the clipboard. (Depending on the style, this could be long and detailed or, if the style demands footnotes, simply a number.)
*   **Copy Selected Items to Clipboard:** Copies the full bibliographic reference for the selected item(s) to the clipboard.
*   **Toggle Tag Selector:** Shows/hides the tag selector.
*   **Mark All Feed Items As Read/Unread:** Marks all items in the selected [feed](/support/preferences/feeds) as read/unread.

Any changes made to this page will only take effect after you restart Zotero. a new browser window is opened.

To configure your Quick Copy preferences, open the Zotero [settings](/support/kb/preferences) and select [Export](/support/preferences/export). From this tab you can do the following:

## Conventions
- Durable notes and decisions go in docs/, committed. Not in chat, not in cloud project docs.
- Documents, data exports, and deliverables live on the primary storage drive (Google Drive 00_Primary_Storage_Drive), not in the repo. Files over 95 MB never go in git.
- `data/` is gitignored except aggregate summaries. Regenerate the file-level manifest with `pwsh scripts/build_manifest.ps1`.
- Codex workers read staged copies in `staging/`, never the Drive root. DexaProject, athlete snapshots, Catapult and PFF exports are never catalogued.
- The ingest review gate has two stages.
  1. Before atomizing, verify the source artifact by an independent route: page order, scanned versus text, transcripts checked against captions.
  2. Before promoting, Codex reviews the staged entries against the staged sources, with instructions to falsify (`staging/review_<source>_codex.md`). Nothing reaches the vault without a GO or a GO AFTER FIXES that has been applied.
- Library entries label every voice. The source author's statements are plain. Eric's judgments get "Eric's review:". The entry writer's own reasoning gets "Inference:". No unlabeled judgments. Every number carries a timestamp or page the reviewer can check, and a claim is only tagged "confirmed in PDF" if that PDF is staged. (Learned from the Harries review, 2026-09-26: 25 of 35 files needed fixes, mostly for attribution.)

--- README head:
# Zotero Research Bridge

A read-only bridge from Zotero into automatically research-grounded, applicability-aware agent conversations and validated
SecondBrain Paper Briefs.

The implementation includes a shared CLI/MCP core, incremental SQLite/FTS Paper Index, normal-question
multi-paper evidence packs, a resumable all-library backlog, page-aware PDF evidence, and validated Knowledge
Promotion. See [setup](./docs/SETUP.md), [the architecture](./docs/DESIGN.md),
[Paper Brief contract](./docs/PAPER_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md), [implementation plan](./docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md),
[ten-paper pilot](./docs/PILOT.md), and [verification status](./docs/VERIFICATION.md).

```powershell
uv sync --extra dev
uv run zotero-bridge configure --user-id 13524464
uv run zotero-bridge doctor
uv run zotero-bridge sync --full
uv run zotero-bridge ground "How should training load inform return to play?"
uv run zotero-bridge backlog --limit 50
uv run zotero-bridge batch-create next-10 --limit 10 --status pending_extraction
uv run zotero-bridge batch-run next-10 --extract
uv run zotero-bridge batch-status next-10
uv run zotero-bridge pages ITEM_KEY --page 3
uv run zotero-bridge publication-candidate ITEM_KEY reviewed-synthesis.json
```

`publication-candidate` requires a current validated Paper Brief and produces a local
`READY_FOR_LIBRARY_REVIEW` JSON artifact. It does not write to, commit, or deploy the public Evidence Library.
See [ADR 0011](./docs/adr/0011-export-reviewed-evidence-library-candidates.md).

--- classification doc head:
# Zotero backlog classification

Second item in the capability map's sequence, after the skill router. Every research
record in the Zotero library gets a topic; when Jev is not confident enough to name
one, it reports the broader domain that topic sits in instead. Nothing is dropped and
nothing queues for review.

Built 2026-09-19 from the `classification_using_confidence` cookbook
(`docs/vendor/typesafe/cookbooks/classification_using_confidence.md`). Code in
`zotero_classify/`.

**Governance: tier A.** Published literature and its metadata only. No athlete data,
no health records, nothing from GPS, force plate, DEXA or S2. The state sent to the
API is a title, a journal, a year and up to 2,000 characters of a published abstract.

## What came out

| | |
|---|---|
| records classified | **1,418** — every eligible research item, reconciled against the bridge's own count |
| named a specific topic | **1,236 (87%)** |
| reported as a domain instead | 182 (13%) |
| taxonomy | 96 topics in 14 domains |
| wall time | **86 seconds**, 8 workers, zero failures |
| cost | about **$0.07** at $0.042 per million input tokens, output free |

Deliverables, regenerate with `python export.py`:

- `zotero_classify/out/zotero_topics.csv` — one row per record: label, how specific it
  is, confidence, and whether it had an abstract. Sorts and filters in a spreadsheet.

# Zotero setup for Flint

Status: diagnosis and recommendations, 2026-10-13. Read-only probes only. No Zotero preferences changed, no plugins installed, no sync run, no skill edited. Each fix below waits for Eric's go-ahead.

Companion memory: `reference_zotero-expert-reference` (Tier A, Mac DEV slug) holds the general Zotero reference.

## 1. Current state (Mac)

- Zotero 10.0.5 at `/Applications/Zotero.app`. Data directory `/Users/kristinarash/Zotero`.
- Library user ID: 13524464.
- Local library: 1,547 regular items, 1,514 PDF attachments. Every PDF has a full-text row (1,514 of 1,514), so local full-text coverage for PDFs is complete.
- 143 regular items have no attachments. These are the metadata-only items.
- Local API is on: `extensions.zotero.httpServer.localAPI.enabled = true`.
- Plugins: Zutilo 4.2.2 only. Better BibTeX is not installed.
- Collection `SecondBrain Queue` (key `NC8TKL4K`): 109 items, 104 with a PDF. Flint docs say 92. Use 109 until a newer count replaces it.

## 2. Three retrieval layers, and which one is live

| Layer | Where | State on this Mac | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Go CLI and MCP, `zotero-research-library-pp-cli` / `-pp-mcp` | `~/go/bin/`, MCP name `zotero` in `~/.claude.json` | Cache last synced 2026-09-02 (about six weeks old). 0 full-text rows. Its "24%" full-text figure comes from this stale cache, not from Zotero. | Stale. Do not use for Flint. |
| B. Bridge, `zotero-bridge` (Python, read-only) | `~/DEV/ZoteroInjestion` (run with `uv run zotero-bridge ...`) | `doctor` reports production-ready. Key has library read and file read, write off. Local API enabled. Index `~/Library/Application Support/zotero-research-bridge/library.db`, 3,792 items at library version 9,575, updated today. Full-text records: 0. | Live. Recommended layer. Needs two fixes (see section 4). |
| C. `zotero-research` MCP | Named in the sports-science skill and in `ZoteroInjestion/docs/VERIFICATION.md` | Not configured on this Mac. Only MCP entry is `zotero` (layer A). | Not available here. |

Naming drift to know about: `research-in-5` calls `sync_zotero_library` and `get_paper`. Those names are not in layer A or the bridge CLI. Treat that skill's Zotero steps as unverified until its MCP source is found. Do not edit the skill to fix the names without the skill-bloat check first.

## 3. Why the numbers disagree

- Flint plan: "861 of 3,570 items have full text." Both numbers come from the stale layer A cache. The live database shows full text for all 1,514 PDFs. Correct the plan's figure when the next STATUS is written.
- Bridge: `fulltext_records: 0`, while its VERIFICATION page recorded 803 full-text records at library version 6,387. The index has moved past that version, and full text has not been refreshed since. Fix: run `zotero-bridge sync --fulltext` (section 4, step 2).

## 4. Fixes in order

Each step is small. Eric approves each one before it runs.

1. **Choose the layer (decision for Eric).** Recommend B, the bridge. It is read-only, it is the layer Flint's count already uses, and it already knows the promotion queue. The other option is A, which is six weeks stale and would need a rebuild first. Decision needed: approve B as the Flint layer.
2. **Refresh the bridge's full-text index.** Command: `cd ~/DEV/ZoteroInjestion && uv run zotero-bridge sync --fulltext`. This writes only the bridge's own index. It does not write to Zotero. Check afterwards with `uv run zotero-bridge doctor` (`fulltext_records` should be near 1,514).
3. **Fix the SecondBrain path.** The bridge config (`~/Library/Application Support/zotero-research-bridge/config.toml`) sets `secondbrain_dir = "/Users/kristinarash/Desktop/SecondBrain"`. That folder does not exist. The vault is `~/SecondBrain`. Change the value to `/Users/kristinarash/SecondBrain`, then re-run `doctor`. This config edit is local only.
4. **Tag convention for Flint routing.** Tags travel across libraries. Collections do not. Proposal:
   - Topic tags that mirror the Jev taxonomy (14 domains, 96 topics in `TypeSafe_Sandbox/zotero_classify/taxonomy.py`), so Drive files and Zotero share one map.
   - A small state set: `flint:candidate`, `flint:approved`, `flint:promoted`. Assign colors to the three so Eric can approve with the number keys.
   - A saved search "Date Added in the last 7 days AND Tag is not flint:*" as the weekly triage view.
   - Flint then keeps its queue state inside Zotero. No second database.
5. **Drive intake route for papers: stored files, not linked files.** Linked files do not sync and do not work in group libraries. Drive reads can hang on this Mac (see the REA and Ghidra traps memory). Copy batches to a local staging folder first, then drag into Zotero. Let Retrieve Metadata run. For leftovers, use right-click > Create Parent Item with a DOI or ISBN. Run Duplicate Items before anything is promoted.
6. **Optional: Better BibTeX.** The bridge and Flint cite by item key, so this is not blocking. Install only if citekey-style citations are wanted later. A plugin has full access to Zotero, so install only with Eric's approval.

## 5. Checks before any step runs

- Zotero preferences to confirm in the UI (not yet seen in `prefs.js`, so defaults apply): "Automatically attach associated PDFs" on; "Sync full-text content" on if cross-device search is wanted; "Automatically take snapshots" on or off as Eric prefers.
- Keep the copy of the Zotero database that was made for probing out of the repo. It was created at `/Users/kristinarash/DEV/_scratch_zotero_probe/` and should be deleted by hand. The delete was blocked by a safety rule.

## 6. Open items

- Count the queue again (109 now, 92 in the plan).
- Find the `zotero-research` MCP source, or retire its name from the skills.
- Decide whether the Windows machine should use the bridge too. Its VERIFICATION notes say `zotero-research` is connected there. Check that before changing any shared setting.

# AGENTS.md

Project: Flint

## What this is
Flint is Claude working as Eric's sport-science, performance, S&C and rehab thought
partner. This repo builds the knowledge base behind that role. It catalogs Eric's
Drive (his own material, TB's Training Info, Landon Evans, courses, papers), routes the
high-value sources into Zotero and the SecondBrain vault, and writes per-discipline
synthesis notes that compare the sources against Eric's own method. It is a side-lane
project, outside the prioritization-slate cap. See `README.md` for the approach and
`docs/PLAN.md` for the checklist.

## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Conventions
- Durable notes and decisions go in docs/, committed. Not in chat, not in cloud project docs.
- Documents, data exports, and deliverables live on the primary storage drive (Google Drive 00_Primary_Storage_Drive), not in the repo. Files over 95 MB never go in git.
- `data/` is gitignored except aggregate summaries. Regenerate the file-level manifest with `pwsh scripts/build_manifest.ps1`.
- Codex workers read staged copies in `staging/`, never the Drive root. DexaProject, athlete snapshots, Catapult and PFF exports are never catalogued.
- The ingest review gate has two stages.
  1. Before atomizing, verify the source artifact by an independent route: page order, scanned versus text, transcripts checked against captions.
  2. Before promoting, Codex reviews the staged entries against the staged sources, with instructions to falsify (`staging/review_<source>_codex.md`). Nothing reaches the vault without a GO or a GO AFTER FIXES that has been applied.
- Library entries label every voice. The source author's statements are plain. Eric's judgments get "Eric's review:". The entry writer's own reasoning gets "Inference:". No unlabeled judgments. Every number carries a timestamp or page the reviewer can check, and a claim is only tagged "confirmed in PDF" if that PDF is staged. (Learned from the Harries review, 2026-09-26: 25 of 35 files needed fixes, mostly for attribution.)
- Writing: plain, direct, no em dashes. Documents use the Baylor design system.

---
name: zotero-expert-reference
description: "Zotero expert reference distilled from zotero.org/support (read 2026-10-13) — collect, organize, search, annotate, cite, sync, back up. Open for any Zotero how-to, troubleshooting, or setup question."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 25cf7597-8d98-41ad-9f32-763c997e5baa
  modified: 2026-10-13T15:13:21.619Z
---

Source: https://www.zotero.org/support/ (read 2026-10-13). Pages read: quick start, adding items, PDF reader, searching, collections and tags, word processor plugins, sync, data directory, attaching files, duplicates, PDF metadata, tips, bibliographies, styles, notes.

## Collect
- Best way to add items: Zotero Connector save button (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari). It pulls metadata and open-access PDFs. Prefer it over manual entry.
- Add by Identifier (toolbar): ISBN, DOI, PubMed ID, arXiv ID, ADS Bibcode. Separate many IDs with spaces, commas, or line breaks.
- Drop a PDF in Zotero: it becomes a standalone attachment and metadata is retrieved automatically. The first few pages go to a Zotero lookup service (Crossref plus DOI/ISBN lookup; no account needed). If that fails: right-click > Create Parent Item (enter DOI/ISBN), or Manual Entry.
- Prefer child attachments under a parent item. Standalone attachments cannot be cited and are not used by My Publications.
- Stored files (default) live in the data directory and Zotero manages them. Linked files (Ctrl/Cmd-drag with modifier, or Attach Link to File) are not synced and do not work in group libraries. Convert with Tools > Manage Attachments.
- Large batches from Google Scholar, ProQuest, or Web of Science: export BibTeX or RIS and import the file. This avoids lockouts.
- Titles: store in sentence case. Zotero converts to title case on output. Journal abbreviations: store with periods.
- Extra field holds custom data. For citing fields Zotero does not support, see the KB article on item types and fields.
- Feeds: RSS subscriptions from journals, to browse and save.

## Organize
- Collections work like playlists. One item can sit in many collections, with no copies made. To move (not copy) between collections: hold Cmd (Mac) or Shift (Win/Linux) while dragging.
- Delete Collection keeps the items. Delete Collection and Items removes both.
- Tags travel between libraries. Collections do not.
- Colored tags (up to 9): press number keys 1-9 to toggle on selected items. Drag items onto a tag in the tag selector to tag them.
- Rename or delete a tag in the tag selector to change it everywhere. Renaming to an existing tag name merges the two.
- Automatic tags (red icon) come from catalog subject headings. Hide them, or delete them library-wide.
- Saved Searches are smart collections that update themselves. Example: Tag is not "read" = a To Read list.
- Special collections: Unfiled Items, Duplicate Items, Trash (30-day default, restorable), My Publications.
- View menu > Show Items from Subcollections.

## Search
- Quick search (Cmd/Ctrl-F) has three modes: Title/Year/Creator; All Fields and Tags; Everything (includes PDF full text). Type a leading quote mark to search only on Enter. This is faster on big libraries.
- Advanced Search (magnifier icon): field filters, Match all or any, Search subcollections, Show only top-level items, Include parent and child items. Wildcard is %, e.g. "W% Shakespeare".
- Saved Advanced Search updates itself. For Boolean logic, save each condition as a saved search, then combine them with a third search: Collection is Condition1 AND Collection is Condition2.
- Full-text index covers PDF, EPUB, HTML, and text files (not .docx). Default limit is 500,000 characters or 100 pages. If an item is missing from "Everything", right-click > Reindex Item. The "Indexed:" field in the right pane shows status.

## Annotate and notes
- PDF reader modes: unlocked (select text, pick a color from the popup) or locked (choose the highlight/underline tool and color; each selection highlights automatically).
- Annotations are stored in the Zotero database, not in the PDF file. External readers will not show them unless you export a PDF with embedded annotations. Adding, rotating, or deleting pages in an external reader breaks annotation positions.
- Get annotations into notes: drag them into the Notes pane, right-click > Add to Note, or right-click the parent item > Add Note from Annotations. Annotation citations link back to the page.
- Child notes attach to an item (Notes tab). Standalone notes come from the New Note button. Notes sync with metadata and do not count against file storage.
- Note editor "..." menu: Show/Hide Annotation Colors, Show/Hide Annotation Citations. Note templates customize annotation output.

## Cite and write
- Word, LibreOffice, and Google Docs plugins ship with Zotero. They insert citations, build the bibliography automatically, and switch styles for the whole document. Reinstall from Cite > Word Processor Plugins in preferences.
- Without a plugin: Quick Copy (drag items into any text field; hold Shift while dragging for in-text citations); Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-C copies the bibliography; Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-A copies a citation; export BibTeX or RIS. The Export pane sets format and HTML markup.
- RTF Scan: write plain text with placeholders, then Zotero finalizes citations and the bibliography.
- Styles use CSL (Citation Style Language). Over 10,000 are in the Zotero Style Repository (zotero.org/styles). For a style error, update Zotero and the style first, then post in the forum titled "Style Error: [Name]".
- Duplicates: Zotero compares title, DOI, and ISBN. Then it checks year (within 1 year) and first-author last name plus first initial. False positives cannot be marked yet. Always merge; do not delete. Merges keep collections and tags, and word-processor citations stay intact. Alt/Option-click selects one item. Merge works on same-type items anywhere in the library.

## Sync and backup
- Data sync is free and unlimited, and covers everything except files. File sync: Zotero Storage (300 MB free, paid tiers; recommended) or WebDAV (not for group libraries).
- Never put the data directory in a cloud-synced folder (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive). It can corrupt the database.
- Default data directory: macOS /Users/<user>/Zotero; Windows C:\Users\<user>\Zotero; Linux ~/Zotero. Find it with Settings > Advanced > Show Data Directory.
- Contents: zotero.sqlite (database), storage/ (one 8-character subfolder per attachment), zotero.sqlite.bak (automatic daily backups), fulltext.sqlite (rebuildable; not backed up). Close Zotero before copying anything. Keep the -wal file with the .sqlite file.
- Backup: use a whole-machine backup such as Time Machine. Do not use export as a backup.
- Restore routes: sync back down; restore a .bak file (rename the current file first); or replace the whole data directory with Zotero closed.
- Replace Online Library (sync reset option) overwrites server data with local data. Use with care.

## Preferences and groups
- General pane: auto-snapshots of web pages, trash period, automatic tags toggle, and the external PDF reader choice.
- Group libraries are shared and separate from personal ones. Duplicate detection runs within each library only.

Source: https://www.zotero.org/support/ (read 2026-10-13). Pages read: quick start, adding items, PDF reader, searching, collections and tags, word processor plugins, sync, data directory, attaching files, duplicates, PDF metadata, tips, bibliographies, styles, notes.

## Collect
- Best way to add items: Zotero Connector save button (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari). It pulls metadata and open-access PDFs. Prefer it over manual entry.
- Add by Identifier (toolbar): ISBN, DOI, PubMed ID, arXiv ID, ADS Bibcode. Separate many IDs with spaces, commas, or line breaks.
- Drop a PDF in Zotero: it becomes a standalone attachment and metadata is retrieved automatically. The first few pages go to a Zotero lookup service (Crossref plus DOI/ISBN lookup; no account needed). If that fails: right-click > Create Parent Item (enter DOI/ISBN), or Manual Entry.
- Prefer child attachments under a parent item. Standalone attachments cannot be cited and are not used by My Publications.
- Stored files (default) live in the data directory and Zotero manages them. Linked files (Ctrl/Cmd-drag with modifier, or Attach Link to File) are not synced and do not work in group libraries. Convert with Tools > Manage Attachments.
- Large batches from Google Scholar, ProQuest, or Web of Science: export BibTeX or RIS and import the file. This avoids lockouts.
- Titles: store in sentence case. Zotero converts to title case on output. Journal abbreviations: store with periods.
- Extra field holds custom data. For citing fields Zotero does not support, see the KB article on item types and fields.
- Feeds: RSS subscriptions from journals, to browse and save.

## Organize
- Collections work like playlists. One item can sit in many collections, with no copies made. To move (not copy) between collections: hold Cmd (Mac) or Shift (Win/Linux) while dragging.
- Delete Collection keeps the items. Delete Collection and Items removes both.
- Tags travel between libraries. Collections do not.
- Colored tags (up to 9): press number keys 1-9 to toggle on selected items. Drag items onto a tag in the tag selector to tag them.
- Rename or delete a tag in the tag selector to change it everywhere. Renaming to an existing tag name merges the two.
- Automatic tags (red icon) come from catalog subject headings. Hide them, or delete them library-wide.
- Saved Searches are smart collections that update themselves. Example: Tag is not "read" = a To Read list.
- Special collections: Unfiled Items, Duplicate Items, Trash (30-day default, restorable), My Publications.
- View menu > Show Items from Subcollections.

## Search
- Quick search (Cmd/Ctrl-F) has three modes: Title/Year/Creator; All Fields and Tags; Everything (includes PDF full text). Type a leading quote mark to search only on Enter. This is faster on big libraries.
- Advanced Search (magnifier icon): field filters, Match all or any, Search subcollections, Show only top-level items, Include parent and child items. Wildcard is %, e.g. "W% Shakespeare".
- Saved Advanced Search updates itself. For Boolean logic, save each condition as a saved search, then combine them with a third search: Collection is Condition1 AND Collection is Condition2.
- Full-text index covers PDF, EPUB, HTML, and text files (not .docx). Default limit is 500,000 characters or 100 pages. If an item is missing from "Everything", right-click > Reindex Item. The "Indexed:" field in the right pane shows status.

## Annotate and notes
- PDF reader modes: unlocked (select text, pick a color from the popup) or locked (choose the highlight/underline tool and color; each selection highlights automatically).
- Annotations are stored in the Zotero database, not in the PDF file. External readers will not show them unless you export a PDF with embedded annotations. Adding, rotating, or deleting pages in an external reader breaks annotation positions.
- Get annotations into notes: drag them into the Notes pane, right-click > Add to Note, or right-click the parent item > Add Note from Annotations. Annotation citations link back to the page.
- Child notes attach to an item (Notes tab). Standalone notes come from the New Note button. Notes sync with metadata and do not count against file storage.
- Note editor "..." menu: Show/Hide Annotation Colors, Show/Hide Annotation Citations. Note templates customize annotation output.

## Cite and write
- Word, LibreOffice, and Google Docs plugins ship with Zotero. They insert citations, build the bibliography automatically, and switch styles for the whole document. Reinstall from Cite > Word Processor Plugins in preferences.
- Without a plugin: Quick Copy (drag items into any text field; hold Shift while dragging for in-text citations); Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-C copies the bibliography; Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-A copies a citation; export BibTeX or RIS. The Export pane sets format and HTML markup.
- RTF Scan: write plain text with placeholders, then Zotero finalizes citations and the bibliography.
- Styles use CSL (Citation Style Language). Over 10,000 are in the Zotero Style Repository (zotero.org/styles). For a style error, update Zotero and the style first, then post in the forum titled "Style Error: [Name]".
- Duplicates: Zotero compares title, DOI, and ISBN. Then it checks year (within 1 year) and first-author last name plus first initial. False positives cannot be marked yet. Always merge; do not delete. Merges keep collections and tags, and word-processor citations stay intact. Alt/Option-click selects one item. Merge works on same-type items anywhere in the library.

## Sync and backup
- Data sync is free and unlimited, and covers everything except files. File sync: Zotero Storage (300 MB free, paid tiers; recommended) or WebDAV (not for group libraries).
- Never put the data directory in a cloud-synced folder (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive). It can corrupt the database.
- Default data directory: macOS /Users/<user>/Zotero; Windows C:\Users\<user>\Zotero; Linux ~/Zotero. Find it with Settings > Advanced > Show Data Directory.
- Contents: zotero.sqlite (database), storage/ (one 8-character subfolder per attachment), zotero.sqlite.bak (automatic daily backups), fulltext.sqlite (rebuildable; not backed up). Close Zotero before copying anything. Keep the -wal file with the .sqlite file.
- Backup: use a whole-machine backup such as Time Machine. Do not use export as a backup.
- Restore routes: sync back down; restore a .bak file (rename the current file first); or replace the whole data directory with Zotero closed.
- Replace Online Library (sync reset option) overwrites server data with local data. Use with care.

## Preferences and groups
- General pane: auto-snapshots of web pages, trash period, automatic tags toggle, and the external PDF reader choice.
- Group libraries are shared and separate from personal ones. Duplicate detection runs within each library only.

## Already on this machine (pointers, not copies)
- MCP tools: mcp__zotero__* (search, items_get, collections_*, cite, export, full_text_deep_search, sql, learnings, playbook).
- Skills: pp-zotero-research-library (library search and sync) and sports-science-research-grounding (research answers and batch work). Use them for procedures; this file is only the reference.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/closeout

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

This one file serves Claude Code, Codex and Cowork (uploaded to claude.ai). Cowork has no TaskList and no Claude Code memory hooks: do what applies there and say what was skipped.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- **Registry drift.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py crosswalk` (`portfolio_json` is in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`). It compares `portfolio.json` with every DEV folder and Drive `01_PROJECTS` folder and only reports; it never moves anything. Do not fix drift during closeout. List each item it found under "Still open", naming any folder created this session first: that is a project started without a row, the exact way projects got lost before the 2026-10-03 organization pass. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive checks never ran; say so, do not call it clean. Cowork cannot run it; say it was skipped.
- **7-day rule.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py seven-day --apply`. Name any project it paused, and any project on its last two days, under "Still open" with what it still needs (a receiver, step 1). Revive with the board's status pill or `portfolio.py` once there is a first step to show.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- **Registry edits get their own commit.** In project-triage, if `git status --porcelain portfolio.json` shows a change (board edits from the day, `set-status`, `set-receiver`), commit that file alone first as `data: board edits <YYYY-MM-DD>`, then the rest. The board header's "N unpushed registry edits" counts these; a skipped one becomes a JSON merge conflict when the other machine edits too.
- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- If `~/.claude/mods` changed this session (a mod added, edited or `.disabled`), run the mods sync (`bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh` on the Mac, `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\mods\mods-sync.ps1` on Windows) and list any invalid mod under "Still open".
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours. On a Cowork-only day it may be absent; say so, it is not an error.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first. Item 1 is one concrete action (a command to run or a file to open), not a theme: it is the line `~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` shows Eric the next morning
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric, each one written out in full as its own top-level bullet: the question itself and enough context to answer it without opening another file. Never a pointer ("See PLAN.md"): `/startup` reads this section across every repo with `where-was-i.py --decisions`, and a pointer gives no question to answer. Mark answered items `ANSWERED <date>: …` or strike them through (`~~…~~`) so they drop off that list. Leave the section empty, not "-", when nothing is waiting.
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

Then run `python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --decisions --days 1`. It prints exactly what tomorrow's `/startup` will show as "Decisions waiting on you". Every decision this session left open must appear there as a readable question; if one is missing or shows as a pointer, fix that repo's `## Open questions` before the commit.

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

**Keep the resume cards true (PM system design Decision 9).** The live board shows each project as a card read from STATUS and the registry; if a card doesn't make sense tonight, it won't in six weeks. Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/landed.py scan --days 1` (about a minute), then `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py card-check`. It prints the card of every registry project touched today, on either machine, with its gaps. Fix each gap before the Step 2 commit:

- `STATUS has no entry dated <today>`: add `- <today>: <what happened>` under the repo's Done / Current state.
- `STATUS has no Next item`: put one concrete action first under `## Next`.
- `no next step (next_action)` (Drive-only row): set it on the board or with `portfolio.py add-update <name> "<note>" --next-action "<step>"`.
- `needs a receiver`: `portfolio.py set-receiver <name> "<who>"` (a name, or `me: <why>`). Ask Eric when it is not obvious from the session; never invent one.
- `touched but marked <status>`: revive it (`portfolio.py set-status <name> active`) or say in STATUS why a retired project was touched.

Re-run `card-check` after the fixes. Its output is the last section of the report (**Cards:**); trim to projects with work today if it is long, but never drop one that still has a gap.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what> / skipped (Cowork, no hooks)
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Registry drift:** <N items, or "none"> (`portfolio.py crosswalk`)
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.

**Cards:** <`portfolio.py card-check` output, after the Step 4 fixes>
```

The cards come last on purpose: they are what the next session, on either machine, picks up from.

"Clear to sign off" means: every touched repo is pushed (or is a declared local-only repo). If anything is unpushed, the verdict is "Not clear" and the unpushed repo is the one thing blocking.

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

**Where everything landed.** Build that list from the ledger, not from memory: the Step 4 `landed.py scan --days 1` already refreshed it (it reads git in every DEV repo and file times on Drive and the vault, so files written by scripts and shell copies are included); run `landed.py show --days 1`. Put its project-grouped output in the report under **Landed:** (trim to the projects this session touched if it is long). The ledger lives in `~/.claude/global-memory/landed/` and is pushed with global-memory, so `/landed` on the other machine shows it too.

## Rules

- Push every touched DEV repo. Do not leave the laptop with unpushed work; the other machine pulls from GitHub, not from this disk.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Purpose

Athletic performance data infrastructure for Baylor University. The primary active project is an automated post-practice GPS report for Football using the Catapult API. ForceDecks integration is a separate, future project.

## Project: `coach_report/`

**Post-session coach report** — high-level planned-vs-actual one-pager for coaches, read-only consumer of `gps_report/data/gps_history.duckdb` (never writes to it). Sections: planned vs actual (Player Load, PL/min, Explosive Efforts vs day-type historical IQR), max-velocity exposure lists, and XmR SPC flags for over-/under-dosed athletes with sparkline control charts. Output: self-contained HTML + PDF under `coach_report/Reports/coach/YYYY-MM-DD/`.

```
cd coach_report
python coach_report.py --date today            # after practice (data must be ingested by gps_report first)
python coach_report.py --date 2026-04-25       # specific date
python -m pytest tests/                        # unit tests
```

Day-type regexes, thresholds, and SPC settings live in `coach_config.yaml`; per-date plan overrides in `plan_overrides.yaml`. Design spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-coach-report-design.md`. Note: the DB column `total_player_load` stores Catapult `average_player_load` (a per-period average; true/stored ratio varies ~5–17× by season — NOT a usable volume metric). coach_report derives **true session Player Load = `player_load_per_minute` × minutes** (verified identical to `pl_low+pl_med+pl_high+pl_veryhigh`, which is the fallback when PL/min is null); this matches AJ's team report exactly. Intensity uses stored `player_load_per_minute` (duration-weighted across multi-session days).

## Active Project: `gps_report/`

**Automated post-practice GPS report** — pulls Football session data from Catapult Connect v6 API, stores summary stats in DuckDB, and generates a self-contained HTML report + plain-text email summary.

### Entry points
```
cd gps_report

# Daily report (after practice)
python run_report.py                          # interactive — picks today's session
python run_report.py --date 2026-03-10        # specific date
python run_report.py --session-id <uuid>      # skip picker
python run_report.py --list-positions         # print Catapult position strings (setup)
python run_report.py --force                  # re-import existing session

# Regular pull — the one command (also runs daily at 06:30 via launchd com.keystone.gpspull)
./pull.sh                                     # import new sessions (--since-db), then coach reports for new dates
```

#!/bin/bash
# One command for the GPS pull — the 10:00 + 16:30 launchd job and the manual run after practice.
#   ./pull.sh
# Imports new Catapult sessions into data/gps_history.duckdb (bulk_import.py --since-db),
# then builds a coach report for each newly imported date. Every run leaves
# logs/last_run.json; failures and long gaps append one line to the alert log that the
# Claude Code SessionStart hook surfaces. Exit code = the import's exit code.
# After an ok/partial import it writes Parquet snapshots of every table to Google Drive
# (export_snapshot.py) so the Windows laptop can read the data. An export failure alerts
# and is recorded in the receipt, but never changes the exit code.
set -u

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO="$(dirname "$HERE")"

# Test-only overrides; defaults are the real paths.
PY="${GPS_PULL_PYTHON:-$HERE/.venv/bin/python}"
COACH="${GPS_PULL_COACH_REPORT:-$REPO/coach_report/coach_report.py}"
COACH_OUT="${GPS_PULL_COACH_OUT:-$REPO/coach_report/Reports/coach}"
RECEIPT="${GPS_PULL_RECEIPT:-$HERE/logs/last_run.json}"
ALERT_LOG="${GPS_PULL_ALERT_LOG:-$HOME/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log}"
STALE_HOURS="${GPS_PULL_STALE_HOURS:-36}"
SNAPSHOT_DIR="${GPS_PULL_SNAPSHOT_DIR:-}"  # empty: $ATHLETE_SNAPSHOT_DIR, else Drive

CONFIG="$HERE/config.yaml"
DB="$HERE/data/gps_history.duckdb"

stamp() { date '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z'; }

alert() {
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$ALERT_LOG")"
  printf '[%s] gps-pull: %s — see %s\n' "$(stamp)" "$1" "$RECEIPT" >> "$ALERT_LOG"
}

if ! cd "$HERE"; then
  alert "error exit=1 cannot cd to $HERE"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[$(stamp)] gps pull start"

# 1. Warn when the last successful pull is older than STALE_HOURS (covers days the Mac was off).
stale_msg="$("$PY" -c '
import json, sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
path, hours = sys.argv[1], float(sys.argv[2])
try:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        data = json.load(f)
except (OSError, ValueError):
    sys.exit(0)  # first run: nothing to compare
last = data.get("last_success_at")
if not last:
    print("no successful pull on record")
    sys.exit(0)
t = datetime.fromisoformat(last)
if t.tzinfo is None:
    t = t.astimezone()
age = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - t).total_seconds() / 3600
if age > hours:

=== BodyWeight plan:
# Normative Bodyweight Standards for College Football
## Project Plan

**Prepared for:** Coaching Staff
**Date:** March 19, 2026
**Scope:** Establish percentile-based bodyweight norms (25th, 50th, 75th, 90th) by position using elite player data from the Big Ten, Big 12, and SEC conferences.

---

## 1. Project Overview

The goal is to build a reference dataset of bodyweights for elite college football players, broken down by position, so coaches can evaluate how their players compare to conference and national norms.

**What "elite" means here:** Only players selected to 1st- or 2nd-team All-Conference (Big Ten, Big 12, SEC) or 1st-/2nd-team All-American (AP and AFCA Coaches) from the 2023, 2024, and 2025 seasons.
=== CoachReport_Prototypes SPEC:
# Implementation Spec — Baylor Weekly Coach Report

**Date:** 2026-08-30 · **Status:** approved design, not yet built
**Reads with:** `PRODUCT.md` (product truth) and `DESIGN.md` (visual system).
Those two documents are normative. This one says how the thing gets built.

Prototype A won the decision round. The prototypes in this folder are the *reference
rendering*, not the production source. This spec turns them into a weekly product.

---

## 0. Decisions this spec makes
=== WeeklyCoachReport README:
# Weekly Coach Report

Two editions of one weekly football report for Baylor — a coaches edition and a
performance/medical edition — built from CFBD and PFF, printed and handed out.

Read `PRODUCT.md` (why), `DESIGN.md` (how it looks and what the charts may claim),
and `SPEC.md` (how it is built) before changing anything.

## Monday

Two commands. The first fills the PFF database, which lives in a separate
project and is never written from here; the second builds the report.
=== house-model README:
# house-model

A college football prediction model we own: projected margin, win probability, and total for FBS games. It blends public ratings (BCFToys FEI, GameOnPaper adjusted EPA, CFB Victory Model) trained on CollegeFootballData history, with a PFF matchup layer added in v2.

The full design is in [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md). Current state is in [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).

Copy everything in the box below into Claude Code, Codex, or any capable LLM, in the folder where you want the project. entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.
